author: Chris Walker
title: New Bill Seeks to Expose What Major Banks Knew Regarding Epstein’s Spending
content:
“We need to know what financial institutions and their executives knew about Epstein,” Rep. Robert Garcia said.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Several members of Congress have submitted new legislation that would require financial regulators and private banking institutions to disclose thus far unreleased transactions made by disgraced financier and accused child sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein.

The Epstein Wall Street Records Act would require federal banking regulators — including the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the Federal Reserve, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and the Comptroller of the Currency — to make public any files relating to how Epstein spent his money. The legislation is needed, sponsors of the bill say, because it’s unclear whether banking institutions were aware of his crimes and may have helped facilitate them.

In addition to Epstein, the bill would require disclosures for “any entity owned or controlled” by Epstein, as well as financial holdings and transactions made by Ghislaine Maxwell, his former girlfriend and accomplice, or associates of the two.

Large private financial entities that could be affected by the bill include Barclays, Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan Chase, Bank of America, and others.

The proposed legislation is sponsored by every Democratic member of the House Oversight Committee, including ranking Rep. Robert Garcia (D-California). Joining in sponsorship of the bill are Sens. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts), Richard Blumenthal (D-Connecticut), and Ron Wyden (D-Oregon). Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Kentucky) is the only Republican signed onto the bill so far.

Garcia explained the justification for the bill by stating:

Jeffrey Epstein used his immense wealth to abuse women and girls for decades. Meanwhile, banks and financial institutions enriched him and themselves by servicing his accounts and helping him move money around. We need to know what financial institutions and their executives knew about Epstein, whether they complied with relevant law, and what regulatory agencies learned.

Warren similarly expressed the need for the bill’s passage.

“The bipartisan Epstein Wall Street Records Act will ensure overdue accountability for the wealthy and well-connected on Wall Street who put profits over people,” she said.

“The Epstein Files Transparency Act forced the Attorney General to release DOJ, FBI, and U.S. Attorney’s Offices’ files,” Massie said, referring to a bill that was passed into law last year. “This bill does the same for bank regulators. Justice for the survivors means following the money.”

During the 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump pledged to release files relating to investigations of Epstein, despite the two of them formerly having a very close friendship. After taking office in January 2025, however, Trump balked at disclosing the records, and harshly criticized anyone pointing out that he was breaking his campaign promise, calling those pushing for the release of the files part of a “hoax” against him.

Only after months of pressure did Trump finally acquiesce, signing into law the Epstein Files Transparency Act. Still, after signing the bill, Trump continued to deride the issue as a “Democrat Hoax.”

After the bill’s passage there continued to be delays in the release of the files, which included many mentioning Trump’s connections to Epstein and sexual allegations against the president. Millions of documents relating to Epstein remain unpublished, with many of those that have been made public featuring heavy redactions, in spite of the law’s demand for greater transparency.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: David Swanson
title: Trump’s Threats to Annihilate Iran
content:
Asia, Endangerment, Immorality, North America, World

By Ivana Nikolić Hughes and Peter Kuznick, World BEYOND War, October 16, 2026

It is not possible to excuse, justify, or condone this kind of rhetoric. The only question is what to do about it.

Of all of the things that Donald Trump has said publicly since returning to the White House, his threats to annihilate Iran are arguably the worst. This is not only because the repeated statements are deeply immoral and illegal–deliberate killing of civilians is a war crime–but because they represent the kind of irresponsible rhetoric that will lead us into a global apocalypse and collapse of not just the Persian nation but human civilization as a whole. It is not possible to excuse, justify, or condone this kind of rhetoric. The only question is what to do about it.

As much as some well-meaning people might want to see nuclear weapons as instruments that ended World War II and have kept the peace ever since, the exact opposite has actually been true. Nuclear weapons brutally murdered a couple of hundred thousand civilians in Hiroshima and Nagasaki and injured and sentenced to years and decades of illness and suffering many hundreds of thousands more. As we have written before, multiple alternatives existed to end the war in 1945. In many ways, the false narrative of the atomic bombings averting an invasion and saving lives has enabled the perpetuation of nuclear weapons, bringing the risks to humanity’s survival to levels previously unimaginable. Turning a brutally violent beginning of the nuclear age into something positive has managed to complicate and obfuscate an issue that should never have been complicated. Nuclear weapons are and have always been immoral. Their possession should be illegal.

Although the end of World War II coincided with the advent of nuclear weapons, and we have technically not fought another world war since, this is merely a correlation. Other significant changes in our world, including the founding of the United Nations, technological and scientific progress, and globalized trade, took place over that same time period. In addition, one has to wonder, whose peace we are talking about. Since 1945, over 20 million people have died in armed conflicts around the world, with up to 50 million more indirect deaths stemming from those conflicts. Today, there are nearly 100 armed conflicts across the planet according to the Geneva Academy, and 25 international armed conflicts involving more than one nation state.

All along, in addition to the deaths and suffering in war zones across the planet and the horrific toll exacted by poverty and inequality, humanity has been waiting almost helplessly for another nuclear weapon to explode by accident, miscalculation, or intention, likely triggering a full-blown nuclear war in which tens or even thousands of nuclear weapons are used. The past eight decades have witnessed numerous incidents in which human wisdom and decency or just plain luck interrupted a course of events that seemed inexorably leading to nuclear war. Nuclear weapons have not brought the peace. Quite the opposite – they threaten what little of it we have each and every day.

And yet, for all of his threats on Truth Social and most recently in the halls of the United Nations, Trump has also stated that nuclear weapons “could destroy the world 50 times over, 100 times over,” calling for “denuclearization.” In fact, two days after his unacceptable statement to “drive [Iran] into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness” at the UN General Assembly in September, Trump suggested to President Xi in DC that there be a nuclear summit between China, Russia, and the United States.

Trump did so knowing full well that Xi’s government’s participation in arms control negotiations is contingent upon China achieving rough parity with the nuclear arsenals of the United States and Russia. This should be pursued not by China continuing to expand its arsenal to the gargantuan size of the U.S. and Russian arsenals, but by the U.S. and Russia reducing theirs to the size of China’s, and adopting China’s demand for an across-the-board no-first-use policy.

title: Osman Kavala: AİHM kararına rağmen yeniden yargılamanın reddi yargıya zarar veriyor
content:
Gezi davasında ağırlaştırılmış müebbet hapis cezası verilen ve 1 Kasım 2017’den bu yana cezaevinde tutulan sivil toplum ve insan hakları savunucusu Osman Kavala, AİHM kararının uygulanmamasına ilişkin açıklama yaptı.


Kavala, İstanbul 13. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’nin “yargının itibarına zarar verdiğini” belirterek şunları söyledi:


“25 Ağustos tarihli AİHM kararında maruz kaldığım yargısal işlemler, adaletin inkârı olarak nitelendirilmişti. Bunun ana nedeni suç işlemiş olduğuma dair bir bulgu olmadan ve olmadığının bilinmesine rağmen hukukun özünü zedeleyen işlemlerle özgürlüğümün kısıtlanmasının sürdürülmesi oldu.


13. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’nin vahim bir insan hakları ihlaline son vermek yerine AİHM’e bireysel başvuru hakkı ve CMK maddelerini keyfi biçimde yorumlayarak yeniden yargılamayı reddetmesi yargının itibarına da zarar veriyor.”


AİHM Büyük Dairesi, 25 Ağustos’taki kararında Kavala’nın özgürlük ve güvenlik, adil yargılanma, ifade ve barışçıl toplanma özgürlüğü haklarının ihlal edildiğine hükmetmişti. Mahkeme, Kavala’nın mümkün olan en kısa sürede serbest bırakılması ve mahkumiyetinin bütün sonuçlarının ortadan kaldırılmasına karar vermişti.


İstanbul 13. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi ise AİHM’e başvuru öncesinde iç hukuk yollarının tüketilmesi gerektiğini savunarak yeniden yargılama talebini reddetti. Mahkeme, AİHM’nin bir temyiz mahkemesi olmadığını ve delillerin değerlendirilmesinin ulusal mahkemelerin yetkisinde bulunduğunu ileri sürdü.


Mahkeme bir kez daha AİHM’nin Osman Kavala kararını tanımadı


13 Ekim 2026


Osman Kavala'nın hapsi


Sivil toplum ve insan hakları savunucusu Osman Kavala, 2013'teki Gezi Parkı protestolarını organize ve finanse ettiği iddiasıyla yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında 18 Ekim 2017'de gözaltına alındı, 1 Kasım 2017'de tutuklandı.


Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi (AİHM), 10 Aralık 2019'da Kavala'nın tutuklanması için makul şüphe bulunmadığına ve tutukluluğunun kendisini insan hakları savunucusu olarak susturma amacı taşıdığına hükmederek serbest bırakılmasını istedi.


İstanbul 30. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi, 18 Şubat 2020'de Gezi davasında Kavala'nın beraatine ve tahliyesine karar verdi. Ancak Kavala, cezaevinden çıkamadan yeniden gözaltına alındı ve farklı suçlamalarla tutuklandı. Beraat kararı daha sonra istinaf mahkemesince bozuldu.


Yeniden görülen Gezi davasında İstanbul 13. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi, 25 Nisan 2022'de Kavala'yı "hükümeti ortadan kaldırmaya teşebbüs" suçundan ağırlaştırılmış müebbet hapis cezasına çarptırdı. Karar, 28 Eylül 2023'te Yargıtay tarafından onandı.


Türkiye'nin 2019 tarihli AİHM kararını uygulamaması üzerine Avrupa Konseyi Bakanlar Komitesi ihlal prosedürü başlattı. AİHM, 11 Temmuz 2022'de Türkiye'nin söz konusu karara uyma yükümlülüğünü ihlal ettiğine hükmetti.


AİHM Büyük Dairesi, 25 Ağustos 2026'da verdiği yeni kararda da Kavala'nın özgürlük ve güvenlik, adil yargılanma, ifade ve barışçıl toplanma özgürlüğü haklarının ihlal edildiğine karar verdi.

author: Aaron Regunberg
title: New Documents Expose Exxon’s Attempt to Suppress Damning Climate Evidence
content:
A paper from 1992 shows the oil company anticipating how the melting of Arctic ice sheets could impact its bottom line.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

“Do you believe that statement’s misleading?”

“All the clauses in there are patently false. And I told them so.”

So reads an exchange from the deposition of Joseph Weissman, an ExxonMobil scientist with the company’s former algae biofuels program. The “patently false” statement in question was a corporate press release claiming algae biofuel was a viable solution to climate change that the company would soon be producing at scale. Extensive reporting has already uncovered how ExxonMobil spent nearly half as much advertising its algae research as it spent on the research itself. But testimony like Weissman’s shows just how clearly the company understood that this much-touted project was, in Weissman’s words, a “dead end.” The goal was not to create a viable alternative energy source, but simply, as one internal memo put it, to make consumers “[b]elieve ExxonMobil is committed to helping solve climate change.”

Weissman’s deposition was taken by the Massachusetts Attorney General’s Office as part of its lawsuit against ExxonMobil alleging consumer protection violations. In an under-the-radar filing in April, Massachusetts disclosed this deposition, as well as a range of other documents it had uncovered, to demonstrate the relevance of additional investigative targets that ExxonMobil had been furiously attempting to shield from discovery. These newly released materials cover a range of topics and time periods, from memos on the company’s more recent deceptive advertising campaigns to evidence of its decades-old climate knowledge.

One of the documents is a 1992 paper, “Climate Change Impacts on Northern Offshore Petroleum Operations,” which analyzes how Exxon’s operations in the Beaufort Sea would be affected by its predictions of a “much thinner ice sheet” and other anticipated effects of global warming caused by the use of its products. The upshot for Exxon: “[I]f ice conditions become less severe as predicted, then offshore petroleum operations will become easier and less costly.” Papers like this, demonstrating ExxonMobil’s sophisticated understanding of the realities of global warming, were produced at the same time the company was ramping up its public efforts to, in its own words, “emphasize the uncertainty in scientific conclusions” on climate change in order to prevent the “development of nonfossil fuel resources.”

Needless to say, the contrast between oil companies’ internal climate knowledge and external climate denial is profoundly damaging to the industry. This helps explain why it is going to such extraordinary lengths to attack these climate cases. These corporations are not just afraid of losing these lawsuits; they’re also afraid of the damning evidence the suits will uncover.

This is the skeleton key for understanding Suncor v. Boulder, the high-profile climate case the Supreme Court heard in early October.

Suncor began in 2018, when Boulder, Colorado, sued fossil fuel companies Suncor and ExxonMobil for damages from climate change and the companies’ lies about their role in fueling it. After the Colorado Supreme Court rejected the defendants’ motion to dismiss the case, Suncor and ExxonMobil — likely terrified of what would happen if Boulder were allowed to have its day in court — asked the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene, repeating a request the fossil fuel industry has made again and again in recent years, alongside parallel efforts to lobby Congress and state legislatures to grant it immunity from all climate-related liability.

There is a reason why oil and gas companies are so desperate to stop these cases by any means before they proceed any further. We have likely seen just a sliver of the evidence they have that shows they’ve spent decades knowingly deceiving the public about climate science, climate harms, and their commitment to climate action. How many more reports are they sitting on like the 1992 paper laying out ExxonMobil’s projected opportunities for profiting off a melting Arctic? How many more internal communications like Weissman’s saying that “all the clauses” in a 2018 press release about ExxonMobil’s signature climate solution were “patently false?” The current offensive isn’t just about defeating the cases. It’s also about preventing the …

title: Italien: Landesweite Arbeitsniederlegungen vom 11. Oktober 2026 bis zum 10. April 2027 für mehr Gesundheitsschutz, Entlohnung und Arbeitnehmerrechte bei Amazon
content:
„

Die Gewerkschaft ALA (Associazione Libera Associates) hat für die Amazon-Belegschaften in Italien vom 11. Oktober 2026 bis zum 10. April 2027 zu landesweiten Mobilisierungsmaßnahmen aufgerufen. Der angekündigte Zeitraum entspricht nicht sechs Monaten ununterbrochenem Streik: Er erlaubt laut Angaben der Gewerkschaft ein- oder zweistündige Arbeitsniederlegungen zu Beginn oder am Ende der Schicht sowie ganztägige Streiks. Die Gewerkschaft fordert Verbesserungen in den Bereichen Sicherheit und Gesundheitsschutz, Vergütung, Arbeitszeitgestaltung und die Achtung der Arbeitnehmerrechte. ALA weist darauf hin, dass der Aufruf eine Reaktion auf Probleme darstellt, auf die sie bereits seit Langem hingewiesen hat, sowie auf die unzureichende Reaktion auf ihre Verhandlungsforderungen. Das flexible System der Arbeitsniederlegungen ermöglicht es, an verschiedenen Standorten und in verschiedenen Schichten zu intervenieren, ohne eine Unterbrechung der Tätigkeit als dauerhaft darzustellen, die es nicht ist

.“ Aus dem span.

Beitrag vom 13. Oktober 2026 der Redaktion von Sindicalismo.org


 (Amazon gegen seine Beschäftigten: Sieben internationale Konflikte zwischen Streiks, Gewerkschaftsbildung und Entlassungen, maschinenübersetzt), siehe auch die A.L.A. dazu:


ALA-STREIK BEI AMAZON: IM MITTELPUNKT DER MOBILISIERUNG

Gesundheit, Arbeitsbedingungen, Vergütung, Arbeitszeiten und Achtung der Rechte

A.L.A. ruft zu einem neuen landesweiten Streik der Beschäftigten der Unternehmen der Amazon-Gruppe auf, da auf die Forderungen nach Verhandlungen nicht eingegangen wurde und die bereits gemeldeten Probleme weiterhin bestehen.


Die Durchführung des Streiks erfolgt gemäß den organisatorischen Vorgaben der Gewerkschaft, die den Beschäftigten regelmäßig über die offiziellen Kanäle von A.L.A. mitgeteilt werden. Dies gewährleistet ein einheitliches Vorgehen, verhindert Verwirrung durch falsche Interpretationen und schützt jeden Streikteilnehmer rechtlich. (..)


Die Entscheidung folgt auf monatelange Meldungen, Forderungen nach Maßnahmen und gewerkschaftliche Initiativen zu Problemen, die ALA täglich an den Arbeitsplätzen erfasst.

.

author: Randi Beers
title: Feeding our family — and the community
content:
Dear Nunatsiaq News,


I am writing to share a story about my father Walter J. Porter of Gjoa Haven, Nunavut, and a tradition of sharing that I have witnessed since I was a girl.


My father is blind, but he remains connected to our Inuit traditions and our community through sharing country food. His son provides him with caribou meat, while other family members help butcher it.


What makes this tradition special is that the meat is for our family, as well as for anybody else. It is placed outside so that community members can take whatever they want. People are welcome to take some home for themselves and their families.


My father is happy to be outside for a while when people gather to collect the meat. There is company outside, and people come and go as they take what they need. It is a simple but meaningful way of bringing people together through sharing.


As far back as I can remember, this has been part of my life. I was little when I first noticed this tradition. My father’s grandchildren now see what sharing means.


Chloe Qirqqut, 2, looks out the window with her brother Antoine Porter, 5, as their grandfather William J. Porter shares caribou meat with community members. (Photo courtesy of Aldina Porter)


To me, this is what Inuit values look like in everyday life. We help one another, share what we have and care for our families and community.


Caribou meat is more than food. It connects us to our land, our culture, our traditions and the generations before us.


I wanted to share my father’s story because acts of kindness deserve recognition. His story shows how family can work together to support one another and how the tradition of sharing country food continues in Gjoa Haven.


Thank you for taking the time to read my letter and for recognizing the people and traditions that make our northern communities special.


Sincerely,


Aldina Porter


Gjoa Haven, Nunavut

content:

Na manhã seguinte à

histórica

 conquista dos trabalhadores brasileiros — o fim da jornada 6×1 —, a

manchete

 do UOL me pega de susto: “Oposição tenta revidar fim da 6×1 com redução da maioridade penal”. Na

Folha

, o destaque foi o mesmo.


Ver as propostas de duas mudanças constitucionais de grande impacto social colocadas lado a lado apenas como bandeiras de candidatos que se contrapõem, soou, para mim, como nova demonstração da

distância entre a imprensa noticiosa e a sociedade brasileira

.


Sim, a aprovação do fim da jornada de 44 horas semanais é também uma vitória de Lula, que encampou a bandeira de uma campanha que

nasceu

 no final de 2023, quando um vídeo no TikTok feito por um balconista de farmácia sobre a vida dos que trabalham duro com um dia de descanso viralizou na internet.


Mas, como reconheceu o presidente, essa é uma campanha “que veio da rua”, “uma conquista histórica do povo trabalhador”.

E que para emplacar terá que contar com a vigilância implacável da sociedade e das instituições, incluindo, claro, a própria imprensa.


Desde que o desabafo do ex-balconista Rick Azevedo, eleito vereador pelo PSOL no Rio de Janeiro no ano seguinte – 2024 —, invadiu as redes, a luta pelo fim da 6×1 ganhou as ruas como legítima aspiração popular. E as manifestações só cresceram depois que a reivindicação se tornou uma PEC, em fevereiro de 2025, por iniciativa da deputada federal Erika Hilton (PSOL) e do deputado Reginaldo Lopes (PT).


Os três políticos — Rick, Erika e Lopes — venceram as últimas eleições para deputado federal e são aliados do presidente Lula, ou seja, é esperado do candidato do PT assumir a proposta, que também ganhou força com a adesão dos sindicatos. Aproveitar o momento eleitoral para emplacar mudanças é uma antiga e eficiente estratégia dos movimentos sociais, agora trazendo o apoio decisivo de Lula e obrigando os partidos de direita e extrema direita — desde o início contrários ao projeto — a aprová-la.


Não faz sentido equiparar essa “conquista histórica do povo trabalhador”, “que veio da rua”, como reconheceu o presidente Lula, a ações “populistas”, como fez o

Globo

, ao encaixá-la entre outras medidas do governo lançadas durante a campanha, que realmente podem ser consideradas “eleitoreiras”, ainda que, no mérito, tenham valor para a população.


O jornalismo tem que se guiar pelo interesse público e isso inclui reconhecer as vitórias da sociedade e denunciar os riscos que determinadas propostas implicam para a democracia e os direitos constitucionais dos cidadãos

, como a redução da maioridade penal, assunto grave demais para ser tratado apenas como um “revide” eleitoral.


Até porque, enquanto a primeira proposta nasceu da mobilização popular, a segunda é fruto de um sentimento de insegurança, ressentimento e também de desinformação da população, explorado por políticos e pela própria imprensa de modo a se tornar majoritário na

opinião pública

, o que, de fato, dificulta o debate.


Mas, como jornalistas, temos que encarar a missão de mostrar o que significa na prática encarcerar adolescentes em cadeias superlotadas onde a revolta e a necessidade de sobrevivência favorecem o recrutamento de jovens pelas facções. Também temos que explicar como essa proposta, além de cruel, é inócua para a segurança pública, onde a esmagadora maioria dos adolescentes é antes vítima do que autora da violência.


Onde está a discussão de interesse público, para além da campanha eleitoral, apontando o risco que isso representa para a Constituição brasileira e para a sociedade, que a imprensa conhece tão bem?


Não sou eu que estou dizendo que reduzir a maioridade penal não reduz crimes — são os especialistas em segurança pública, diversas vezes entrevistados pelos jornais. Não é equilibrado publicar críticas substantivas de estudiosos como opinião e retratar um debate tão complexo como se fosse contraposição de dois lados representados como caricaturas: os “linha-dura” e o “povo dos direitos humanos”. Como o debate vai evoluir partindo de ponto equivocado?


Aliás, a imprensa deveria estar mais preocupada com ética do que nunca, quando sua credibilidade foi colocada em xeque pelas últimas revelações sobre Daniel Vorcaro, que atingem alguns veículos em cheio – e sabe-se lá quantas mais virão.


Além …

title: Automatisierung in der Logistikbranche am Beispiel Amazon
content:
Dossier


„

Forscher der TU Berlin haben mit ihrem Roboter die „Picking Challenge“ des Onlinehändlers Amazon gewonnen. Was der Wettbewerb für die Zukunft des Online-Riesen und seine Angestellten bedeutet

.

(…) Mit dem Wettbewerb verfolgt der Online-Händler ein ganz konkretes Ziel: Die möglichst vollständige Automatisierung seiner Logistik. Will Amazon mit der steigenden Zahl der Bestellungen und den wachsenden Anforderungen der Kunden mithalten, muss es die Abläufe in den Logistikzentren effizienter machen. Noch verfeinert der Konzern dazu vor allem das Einlagerungssystem und optimiert den Einsatz der Mitarbeiter – so weit, dass sich manche von ihnen schon als „Roboter“ fühlen

…“

Artikel von Andreas Menn und Stephan Happel vom 29. Mai 2015 in der Wirtschaftswoche online

Indien, USA und Großbritannien…: Amazons Investitionen in die KI-Infrastruktur kosten massiven Stellenabbau und bei der Unfallquote den Mythos der „sicheren Automatisierung“


Amazon gegen seine Beschäftigten: Sieben internationale Konflikte zwischen Streiks, Gewerkschaftsbildung und Entlassungen


„

Der multinationale Konzern Amazon sieht sich mit sieben Arbeitskonflikten konfrontiert, die zeigen, wie seine Belegschaften versuchen, sich angesichts von Produktionsrhythmen, Untervergabe, mangelnder Anerkennung der Gewerkschaften und Entlassungen zu organisieren. In Italien hat eine neue Streikwelle begonnen; in den USA kommt es zu Arbeitsniederlegungen und Gewerkschaftskampagnen; in Deutschland und Großbritannien dauern langwierige Arbeitskämpfe an; und ein weiterer Personalabbau betrifft die USA, Indien und Großbritannien. Es handelt sich um unterschiedliche Konflikte mit unterschiedlichen Zeitpunkten, Forderungen und Situationen, die jedoch alle mit demselben Unternehmen in Verbindung stehen. (…)


USA, Indien und Großbritannien: eine weitere Entlassungswelle

Die Stellenkürzungen folgen auf einen weitaus umfangreicheren Abbau von rund 30.000 Stellen, der im Jahr 2025 begann und bis Januar 2026 andauerte. Die Betroffenen müssen mit dem Verlust ihres Arbeitsplatzes rechnen, während der Konzern einen Teil seiner Geschäftstätigkeit weiter umstrukturiert. Das Fazit

author: anred
title: «¡Son infiltrados!»: acusar y deslegitimar la autodefensa popular
content:
Imagen: Germán Romeo Pena (@germanromeopena)


Cada vez que una movilización responde a la represión con piedras, barricadas o acciones de resistencia, reaparece una explicación que parece resolverlo todo: «son infiltrados». No puede haber una respuesta automática: la presencia de agentes policiales de civil en las protestas es una realidad documentada, pero no alcanza para explicar todas las acciones de resistencia. Detrás de esa simplificación queda una pregunta: ¿por qué cuesta tanto reconocer que también hay sectores populares dispuestos a enfrentar la violencia estatal?

Por ANRed.


La escena se repite. Una movilización multitudinaria reclama por sus derechos. La policía avanza con gases, balas de goma, golpes y detenciones. Un grupo de manifestantes responde con piedras, intenta levantar barricadas o enfrenta el avance de las fuerzas represivas. Inmediatamente, aparece la explicación: «son infiltrados, no son de los nuestros», como aseguró C5N toda la tarde y repitieron otros medios. La sospecha puede tener fundamento en determinadas circunstancias. Los servicios de inteligencia y las fuerzas de seguridad han utilizado históricamente agentes de civil y mecanismos de infiltración para vigilar, perseguir y desarticular organizaciones populares.


Imagen: Germán Romeo Pena (@germanromeopena).


 


El problema comienza cuando la hipótesis se convierte en una certeza sin pruebas y se aplica automáticamente a cualquier manifestación de resistencia. Es necesario no quedar atrapados entre dos explicaciones excluyentes: que toda acción violenta es una operación policial o que cualquier forma de resistencia debe reivindicarse sin discusión. Existe una tercera posibilidad que suele quedar fuera del debate: que haya militantes y manifestantes que decidan actuar por cuenta propia frente a una represión que consideran intolerable o, en este caso, el avance de la entrega total con medidas tales como el DNU 70/23, como se vio con grupos que también de forma colectiva y coordinada actuaban para ahogar los gases lanzados, en medio de una masiva protesta que mezcló el reclamo en defensa por la educación pública universitaria con el reclamo contra el desfinanciamiento en discapacidad y el abandono de las familias endeudadas, y las banderas por la soberanía de Malvinas, con banderas argentinas, palestinas y whipalas.


Guido Piotrkowski, fotógrafo de Página/12, registró cómo le apuntaban directo y tiraban desde la PFA. Le dieron en el pecho, y a un colega que estaba con él en las piernas. El país en el que Javier Milei asegura que «no odiamos demasiado a los periodistas».


La historia desmiente las explicaciones fáciles. Uno de los ejemplos más contundentes que recupera Pablo Solana es la Masacre de Avellaneda del 26 de junio de 2002, cuando en medio de una brutal represión, la Policía Bonaerense asesinó a Darío Santillán y Maximiliano Kosteki. Durante la resistencia popular hubo piedrazos contra la policía, barricadas, vehículos incendiados y otros hechos de enfrentamiento. En su reconstrucción de aquellos acontecimientos, Solana explica que, aunque se documentó la participación de policías de civil y de un expolicía que actuó como parapolicial, la investigación no encontró que las fuerzas de seguridad hubieran provocado la mayoría de los destrozos atribuidos a los manifestantes.


Choque entre organizaciones piqueteras y fuerzas policiales bonaerenses, el día de la Masacre de Avellaneda, el 26 de junio de 2002. Foto: Enrique Cabrera (Télam).


La diferencia es fundamental: comprobar que había agentes de civil no significa demostrar que cada acción de resistencia era una provocación. En aquel caso, la experiencia de investigación sobre los crímenes de Darío y Maxi llevó a una conclusión distinta de la que algunos sectores habían sostenido inicialmente: buena parte de los enfrentamientos había sido protagonizada por militantes que resistían el avance represivo.


Solana también recupera otros momentos de la historia argentina en los que la confrontación callejera fue parte de procesos de lucha popular. El Cordobazo de 1969, con barricadas y enfrentamientos que desbordaron la capacidad represiva de la dictadura de Onganía, es uno de ellos.


Imagen de la resistencia popular durante el Cordobazo.


También las jornadas de diciembre de 2001, cuando las protestas, los saqueos, las barricadas y los enfrentamientos acompañaron la caída del gobierno de Fernando de la Rúa.


20 de diciembre de 2001 en Buenos Aires.


Otro antecedente …

author: Daron Letts
title: Esthetician prepares for New York Fashion Week
content:
Odette Wills wasn’t allowed to wear makeup as a teenager.


Now, the 26-year-old Iqaluit esthetician is preparing to work as a makeup artist backstage at New York Fashion Week, from Feb. 12 to 14.


“I still think I have a long way to go,” Wills said during an interview in her new home-based Authentic Glow Studio which opened in May, the product of a New Year’s resolution.


Wills travelled to New York City for a week in September, where she completed a course at Aimakeup Beauty Academy in Westside Manhattan’s Chelsea neighbourhood and

befriended Instagram influencer Ipek.


“Odette is very talented,” said Aiyma, the school’s founder who goes by one name, in a phone interview Tuesday.


New York Fashion Week, held in February and September every year, features fashion industry shows throughout Manhattan and marks the debut of many international labels.


In the fall, Aiyma’s students (not including Wills) provided makeup for models working with brand labels such as Geo in Style, F&W and Amari Carter, among others.

In December, Wills will learn what brands she will be working with, Aiyma said.


After the course ended, Wills returned north with buoyed confidence, a suitcase packed with new supplies and a plan for expanding her business.


She has added exfoliating, cleansing, and non-medical facial massage to her studio’s services.


As her wait list grows, she said, so will she. She’s planning to take a manicure certification course next.

title: 20th Year of the Kurdish Conference releases final resolution
content:
The 20th conference was held on 14–15 October at the European Parliament in Brussels, organized by the European Union Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC) in cooperation with The Left Group, the Greens/European Free Alliance (Greens/EFA), and the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D).


The final resolution, titled 

20 Years of EUTCC Conferences – 20 Demands for Peace and Democracy

, reads as follows:


"The Annual International Conference on the EU, Turkey, the Middle East and the Kurds, hosted by the EU Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC) in cooperation with the Left Group, the Greens-European Free Alliance (GREENS/EFA) and the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D), was successfully held on 14th and 15th of October 2026 in the European Parliament in Brussels.


The 20th EUTCC Conference looks back on two decades of continuous work for democracy, human rights, the rule of law, a peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question and a European future for Türkiye. Founded in 2004 to provide critical monitoring of Turkey’s EU accession process, the EUTCC’s mission remains as relevant as ever twenty years on.


The conference notes that Turkey continues to face a fundamental democratic choice. At the same time, the current process aimed at ending the armed conflict and finding a political solution to the Kurdish question presents a historic opportunity. Abdullah Öcalan’s statement of February 2025, the subsequent developments surrounding the dissolution of the PKK and the call for a democratic society have opened up a new perspective. 


The EUTCC therefore calls on the European Union, its Member States, the Council of Europe and the Turkish institutions to implement the following 20 steps:


1.  Peace through political dialogue: The peace process must continue on a democratic and legally secure basis.


2.  An end to the isolation on Imralı: Unrestricted access to Abdullah Öcalan must be guaranteed.


3.  Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan: Abdullah Öcalan must be granted his fundamental political, legal and communication rights without delay. His free participation in the peace process is of central importance to its success.


4.  Implementation of the ECtHR judgments: Türkiye must implement all relevant judgments of the European Court of Human Rights fully and without delay, including the right to hope. 


5.  Removal of the PKK from the EU’s list of terrorist organisations: In order to strengthen a sustainable peace process, the European Union should review the inclusion of the PKK on ist list of terrorist organisations and remove the organisation from the list.


6.  Legal foundations for the peace process: The Turkish Government and Parliament must immediately establish the legal and constitutional conditions necessary for a lasting political solution.


7.  Release of political prisoners: All individuals who have been persecuted and imprisoned for carrying out political, journalistic or human rights activities must be released.


8.  Protection of democratic parties: The right to political organisation and parliamentary representation must be guaranteed. Parties must not be forced out of the political arena through bans, criminal proceedings or administrative measures.


9.  End to state-appointed trustees: Democratically elected mayors must be able to carry out their duties freely. The systematic appointment of state-appointed trustees must be brought to an end.


10. Strengthening the rule of law: The independence of the judiciary, fair trials, the separation of powers, and the independence of public prosecutors’ offices and courts must be restored.


11.  Democratic constitutional reform: Türkiye needs a new democratic social contract that guarantees the equality of all citizens, the plurality of society, and the political, cultural and linguistic rights of all population groups.


12.  Kurds as citizens with equal rights: Kurdish identity, language and culture must be fully recognised and protected. A lasting solution to the Kurdish question can only be based on equality.


13.  Women as agents of peace: Women must be involved on an equal footing at all levels of the peace and democratisation process. The conference particularly recognises the central role of Kurdish women in the region’s democratic and peace movements.


14.  Protection of civil society and the media: Journalists, academics, human rights defenders and civil society organisations must be able to work free from state repression …

title: Hasakah tensions: Are Kurds and Arabs being drawn into conflict?
content:
Rising tensions in Hasakah (Hesekê) in the first days of October 2026 have once again raised concerns about the future of Rojava. Clashes between security forces and protesters were reported in the city on 9 October, with several Kurdish youths reportedly injured. Around the same time, pro-government Arab demonstrators held protests against the Kurdish administration, while counter-protests followed attacks on Kurdish symbols.


The Governor of Hasakah blamed the incidents on groups opposed to the integration agreement. However, this statement does not mean that all those involved in the incidents, or their motives, have been conclusively identified.


To view these developments simply as a dispute that has arisen naturally between Arabs and Kurds would be to overlook their political dimensions.


Hasakah is a strategic city where Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs and other communities live together, and where the future of security and administrative structures is being debated. A large-scale conflict here might not remain confined to a single neighbourhood or city. It could directly affect Rojava's political future, relations between its peoples and the integration process with the Damascus administration.


The central issue, therefore, is not to deny the genuine problems that exist between communities, but to question who is exploiting these problems, under what political circumstances and for what purposes.


1. Why do Kurds face a new challenge whenever their political status is discussed?


Kurds in Syria faced serious discrimination concerning their identity, language and citizenship rights for many years under Ba'ath rule. The weakening of central authority following the outbreak of the civil war in 2011 created opportunities for new forms of political and social organisation to emerge under Kurdish leadership in North and East Syria.


During the struggle against ISIS, the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) became one of the international coalition's key local partners. Throughout this period, Kurds gained significant experience not only in military affairs but also in governance, women's participation in social life and the establishment of local institutions.


However, transforming the administrative authority established on the ground into a permanent political status guaranteed by the constitution has proved far more difficult.


The integration process between Damascus and the SDF in 2026 has therefore become a decisive stage. The process concerns not only the incorporation of armed forces into state institutions but also fundamental issues such as the powers of local administrations, security structures, language rights and the management of resources. Disagreements over these matters have heightened concerns within Kurdish society that the gains achieved could be lost.


The historical contradiction is clear: while the role played by Kurds in the struggle against ISIS has gained international recognition, how the political and social gains resulting from that struggle will be protected remains unresolved.


The Kurdish demand is not simply for recognition of their past struggle. The central issue is securing a political order in which they can continue to exist with their own language, identity and democratic institutions.


2. The historical background of Turkey's Rojava policy


 To understand Turkey's approach to Rojava, it is not enough to examine the issue solely through current statements concerning security. 


Ankara maintains that the Kurdish-led armed groups in northern Syria are linked to the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and opposes their establishment as a permanent military and political force along its border. This approach has long been a defining element of Turkey's policy towards Syria. Turkey's military interventions and policies aimed at shaping local balances of power have also been guided by this position.


 However, the issue has broader implications for Kurds. 


The Kurdish question in Turkey and the issue of Kurdish political status in Syria are not legally identical. Nevertheless, developments in the two countries can influence one another. Progress towards peace and a democratic solution in Turkey cannot be considered independently of discussions concerning the future of Kurds in Syria. This creates a significant contradiction: on the one hand, there are efforts to end armed conflict and seek a political solution; on the other, there are serious disagreements over the future of the …

title: Abdullah Öcalan sends message to Jineolojî Conference: A new process lies before us today
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference has begun. Over the course of three days, participants will assess a decade of Jineolojî work in Europe, discuss Jineolojî’s role in building society, and debate a new organizational model for the coming period.


Held in Haelen, the Netherlands, under the slogan

“Bi Jineolojî ber bi avakirina jiyana komunal û azad”

 (“Towards the construction of a free, communal life through Jineolojî”), the conference brought together more than 100 delegates from Switzerland, Germany, France, the Netherlands, Belgium, England, Ireland, Spain, and Italy. The delegates include representatives of Jineolojî committees, women’s councils and communes, mothers of martyrs, youth, culture and the arts, the press, faith communities, and academia.


Photographs of prominent figures in the women’s freedom struggle were displayed in the conference hall, including Sakine Cansız, Zeynep Kınacı, Nagihan Akarsel, Besê Anuş, Viyan Soran, Hevrîn Xelef, Zîlan Pepule, Yadê Eqîde, Alina Sanchez, and Ellen Jaedicke.


The conference opened with a short performance by artist Sosin, accompanied by music and symbolizing women’s solidarity, followed by a moment of silence in memory of the martyrs of the women’s freedom struggle. Jineolojî Academy member Elif Kaya then delivered the opening address.


Abdullah Öcalan sends a message to the conference


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261016112340_2026-10-16-haelen-avrupa-jineoloji-konferansi-abdullah-ocalan-mesaji_1.mp4


Kurdish people's leader Abdullah Öcalan sent the following message to the conference: 


"Dear comrades,


The bearers of Jineolojî’s consciousness and labour,


The builders of a free life,


Ever since my childhood, I have carried a quest within me: to witness the free existence of women and to carve out a living space worthy of them. This quest deepened further when my playmates were taken away from their games and my sister was sent off to work in a sack of bulgur. I saw that liberation was possible in the silent resistance of the village women and in the rise of those who remained of the goddesses; I, too, pursued that belief. I always followed in their footsteps. For I knew that society’s deepest wound was the enslavement of women. Without understanding this, neither freedom, nor equality, nor true democracy could be possible.


When I introduced Jineolojî, my aim was not merely to coin a term. Redefining women’s existence in terms of its historical and social reality; liberating them from objectification and establishing them as subjects—this would be our most vital task to bequeath to history. I wanted to bring to light once more the wisdom of the goddess, which had been obscured by thousands of years of patriarchal civilisation, and the woman-centred way of life of the Neolithic era. The dagger in society’s back was the enslavement of women; without removing this dagger, no social problem could be resolved at its root. Jineology was born as a science that identifies this dagger, rips it out by the roots, and replaces it with the knowledge of a free life.


The efforts expended, the writings, the debates and the organising carried out in the name of Jineolojî to date have demonstrated that this science is, at the same time, a way of life. It served as a breath of fresh air for the women’s perspective. The liberation of women’s identity from sexist moulds, the creation of a space for independent thought and action, and the writing of their own history constituted the most vital task and duty to be bequeathed to human history. These have become the fundamental areas of focus and forms of struggle for Jineolojî. The maxim ‘One is not born a woman, one becomes a woman’ is important. However, this becoming must take place not within the boundaries imposed by men, but through women’s own inner strength. That is why we have said that every woman must have a space of her own, her own voice and her own knowledge.


As a man, I have constantly questioned and renewed myself throughout this process. We have given meaning to this and aimed to break free from centuries of male dominance. I have stated that the fundamental principle of socialism is women’s freedom. For the measure of whether a man can truly be a socialist lies in his ability to establish a correct, equal and free relationship with women. In most of history’s great socialist experiments, this principle was lacking. That deficiency led to the revolutions remaining incomplete. I strove to …

title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards attack Kurdistan highlands with heavy weapons
content:
The Kurdistan Human Rights Network reported heavy artillery shelling and drone attacks by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on parts of the Shaho Mountains in the Dasht-e Qalb area.


According to the report, over the past two days, IRGC forces have deployed heavy military equipment and drones around the village of Daleh Marz and subjected parts of the Shaho Mountains in the Dasht-e Qalb area to artillery shelling and aerial bombardment.


Reports also say that the IRGC has prohibited access to this area on the slopes of the Shaho Mountains in recent days. In addition to extensive artillery shelling, IRGC forces have targeted parts of the area with suicide drones.


These military exercises and artillery attacks are taking place despite the fact that the Shaho and Kosalan Mountains were designated as protected areas under the management of Iran’s Department of Environment in 2009, pursuant to Resolution No. 303 of the Supreme Council for the Environment.


Earlier, in early September of this year, IRGC forces also heavily shelled the Shaho mountain heights near villages in Kamyaran County. The shelling caused fires across a large section of the mountain range.


Environmental activists say that since 2007, IRGC forces have established several military bases in the protected Shaho and Kosalan areas under the pretext of countering the presence of Kurdish opposition parties’ forces. Parts of these areas have also caught fire during military and security exercises conducted by the IRGC.


The activists further state that, despite protests, sections of the region’s pastures and forests have been destroyed during the construction of military bases and roads. According to them, IRGC forces also deliberately set fire to grasslands and vegetation surrounding some of their military facilities. The stated purpose of these actions is to prevent Kurdish opposition forces from using the area’s vegetation as cover when carrying out attacks.

title: Bahadır Özgür adli kontrolle serbest bırakıldı
content:
Fon yolsuzluğuyla ilgili haberleri nedeniyle dün akşam (15 Ekim) gözaltına alınan Halk TV yazarı Bahadır Özgür emniyetteki işlemlerinin ardından bugün İstanbul Adliyesi’ne sevk edildi.


Özgür, emniyetteki ifadesinde fon vurgunu soruşturmasını uzun süredir takip ettiğini ve 30 yıldır gazetecilik yaptığını söyledi. "Soruşturmanın gizliliğini ihlal" suçlamasını reddederek şunları söyledi:


Söz konusu haber sadece bir sosyal medya paylaşımı değil, pek çok medya kuruluşunda yer alan bana ait bir haberdir. Haberde iddia edildiği gibi savcılığın gizlilik kararı koyduğu herhangi bir evrak ya da belge yer almamaktadır. KVKK kapsamındaki veya gizli hiçbir bilgi haberde yoktur. Haberin kapsamı Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek’in açıkladığı 141 kişilik en çok kazananlar listesine dahildir. Bakan Gürlek böyle bir listenin olduğunu bizzat televizyonda kendisi açıklamıştır. Ben de listenin içeriğine yönelik değil, Bakanın açıklaması doğrultusunda haberi yaptım.


Haberde adı geçen tek kişinin eski AKP Genel Başkan Yardımcısı Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya olduğunu belirten Özgür, bu ismin de resmi makamlarca daha önce kamuoyuna duyurulduğunu ve ifadesi alınan bir şüpheli olduğunu anlattı. Savcılığın 29 kişinin tedbir listesine sehven eklendiğine dair yazısını haberleştirdiğini belirterek, amacının kamuoyunu doğru bilgilendirmek olduğunu kaydetti.


Savcılık, Özgür’ün adli kontrol ve yurt dışına çıkış yasağı talebiyle sulh ceza hakimliğine sevk etti.


Hakimlik, dosya üzerinden yaptığı incelemenin ardından Özgür’ün haftada iki gün imza vermesi ve yurt dışına çıkmaması koşuluyla serbest bırakılmasına hükmetti.


Özgür, İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nın yürüttüğü fon soruşturması kapsamında “soruşturmanın gizliliğini ihlal” iddiasıyla gözaltına alınmıştı.


Özgür, 13 Ekim’de yayımladığı haberinde, başsavcılığın aralarında eski bakan Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ve eşi İlyas Kaya’nın da bulunduğu 141 kişilik malvarlığı tedbiri listesini ilgili kurumlara gönderdiğini, daha sonra listedeki 29 kişinin adının “sehven” yer aldığının bildirildiğini yazmıştı.


Gözaltının ardından Özgür’ün 163 bin takipçili X hesabına da erişim engeli getirildi.


Gazeteci Bahadır Özgür gözaltına alındı

title: Rusya, Avrupalı şirketlerin varlıklarına el koydu
content:
Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin’in yayımladığı kararnameyle bazı Avrupalı şirketlerin varlıkları geçici devlet yönetimi altına alındı.

DW Türkçe’nin haberine göre şirketler arasında Alman ambalaj üreticisi Menshen, Fransız zemin kaplama üreticisi Tarkett, İsveçli ambalaj şirketi Sverige International Holdings ve Belçikalı hijyen ürünleri üreticisi Ontex de yer aldı. Ayrıca aralık 2024’te ABD’li ambalaj devi Sonoco tarafından satın alınan eski Avrupa metal ambalaj şirketi Eviosys’in Rusya’daki varlıkları da kararname kapsamına alındı.

Putin’in kararnamesi, Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı Volodimir Zelenskiy’nin Brüksel’de düzenlenen AB zirvesinde yapacağı konuşmanın hemen öncesine denk geldi.

Rusya daha önce de benzer adımlar atmış ve bu tür önlemlerin AB ülkelerinin “savaş alanındaki doğrudan düşmanca faaliyetlere” katılımına bir yanıt olduğunu bildirmişti. Moskova, söz konusu tedbirlerin “geri döndürülebilir” olduğunu da vurgulamıştı.

Moskova geçen ay da gıda devi Nestle ile perakende zincirleri Auchan ve Metro’nun Rusya’daki varlıklarını geçici olarak devlet yönetimine almıştı.

title: TJK-E condemns attacks in Hasakah
content:
In a written statement, the Kurdish Women’s Movement - Europe (TJK-E) said: “The attack on images displaying photographs of fallen YPJ fighters and pioneers of the women’s revolution in Hasakah (Hesekê) is an expression of the ISIS mentality. This despicable attack clearly demonstrates that misogyny and fascism are two sides of the same coin.”


The statement continued: “In recent days, the escalating attacks targeting Kurdish institutions and symbols in Giwêran, south of Hasakah, have followed a systematic pattern. These are not spontaneous incidents, but provocative acts deliberately orchestrated as part of a plan. Through this dirty scheme, the aim is both to provoke conflict between Kurds and Arabs and to pave the way for further attacks against the Kurds. Ultimately, the goal is to eliminate the possibility of peaceful coexistence among peoples based on democracy and equality and to re-establish a homogenizing, monolithic order.”


The statement added: “It is neither ordinary nor coincidental that the symbols and values of the women’s revolution have been targeted in these attacks, carried out by proponents of this monolithic mentality, who also use the ISIS mask. Quite the contrary. In Rojava and North and East Syria, women have led both the defeat of ISIS and the construction of a democratic system for all peoples. In this new phase of the struggle, women continue to uphold their claim to leadership and their mission, take on important responsibilities, and insist on building a democratic system in opposition to the monolithic mentality. This is why their symbols and values are being attacked in such despicable and cowardly ways.


As the European Kurdish Women’s Movement, we regard the recent attacks against the institutions, symbols, and values of the Kurdish people in Hesekê and various other parts of Rojava—including, above all, the attack targeting women’s leadership, organization, and self-defence—as part of an extremely dangerous plan.”


The statement condemned “the forces behind these provocative attacks. We call on all democratic forces, particularly women, to stand against these attacks targeting the Kurds in Rojava and seeking to eliminate the possibility of a democratic Syria in which all peoples enjoy equal rights.”

title: Grape harvest tradition continues despite drought in Amed
content:
As the weather turns colder, villagers have begun the grape harvest. Grapes are being gathered for winter preparations in vineyards where yields have declined year after year due to the climate crisis and worsening drought across the region. Traditional preparations, particularly in Mardin (Mêrdîn) and Diyarbakır (Amed), continue for days, with women carrying out most of the work.


Residents of Hazro (Hezro) said they were producing less grape molasses than in previous years because of declining yields, adding that recent rainfall had also damaged the grapes.


 


Women taking part in the grape harvest in Dercal village, in the Hazro district of Diyarbakır, spend days preparing food for winter. They gather the grapes, crush them to extract the juice and then boil it. They use the grape juice to make molasses, pestil (dried fruit sheets) and cevizli sucuk (walnuts coated in thickened grape juice). The women leave the products they have prepared through hours of labour to dry in the sun. Villagers rely on these foods throughout the winter.


Remziye Ödüngit has been going to the vineyards with her children every September or October for nearly 30 years to harvest grapes. She spends around a week working during the harvest. Although everyone contributes, Ödüngit said women take on greater responsibilities. She expressed her deep love for her village and land, saying she would continue producing for as long as she could.


She refuses to abandon her land


Remziye Ödüngit said they were forced to leave their village during the village evacuations of the 1990s but never gave up their land. They eventually returned and resumed cultivating their vineyards and gardens. She recalled that their vineyards once produced much larger harvests, but over time the vines began to dry out and grape yields declined. Ödüngit said the harvest was shrinking with each passing year.


Ödüngit also said: “We used to harvest much more from our vineyards. Now our vines have dried out and our yields have fallen. The recent rain also damaged the grapes. The harvest gets smaller every year. We used to stay for more than a week, but now we stay for a week and then return. We work until sunset. It is not easy; we put a great deal of effort into it. We pick the grapes and prepare our food for winter. These products sustain us throughout the winter. We do not make them only for ourselves; we also share them with people around us.”


‘Our hard work sustains us through the winter’


Remziye Ödüngit explained how they prepare grape molasses and walnut-filled grape sweets after gathering the grapes during the harvest.


Ödüngit said: “We pick the grapes and crush them to extract their juice. Then we boil the grape juice in large cauldrons to make molasses. To make cevizli sucuk, we thread walnuts onto strings, dip them into the grape mixture we have prepared and leave them to dry. All of this requires hard work. We spend days preparing everything, but during the winter we eat the food we have made ourselves. 


Every villager here does the same thing each year. Some people buy these products from elsewhere or sell them, but we make them for ourselves or give them to people who need them. I love my village and my land very much. No matter how tired we get, being here makes us feel good.”

title: Kurdish Friendship Group established in Australian parliament
content:
The establishment of the Parliamentary Friends of the Kurdish People Group was announced at an event held in the New South Wales (NSW) Parliament in Australia. The group's formation, bringing together 11 MPs from the Greens, Labor and Liberal parties, was celebrated with a ceremony at Parliament.


The event was attended by representatives of the Labor Party, Greens, Liberal Party and Socialist Alliance, as well as the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), Kurdistan National Congress (KNK), Federation of Democratic Kurdish Societies in Australia (FDKS-A), Democratic Kurdish Community Centre (DKTM), PEN Sydney and Sydney Kurdish Youth Association.


Representatives of the Druze, Armenian, Yazidi, Tamil and Myanmar communities, along with numerous civil society organisations, also attended the event.


 


‘The saying that we have no friends but the mountains is beginning to change’


Baran Söğüt, spokesperson for the Diplomacy Commission of the Federation of Democratic Kurdish Societies in Australia, delivered the opening speech.


Söğüt highlighted the historical significance of establishing the Kurdish Friendship Group and said:


“It is a great honour and privilege for me to celebrate the official establishment of the Parliamentary Friends of the Kurdish People Group within the Australian Parliament. We extend our heartfelt thanks to the esteemed members of parliament who have contributed to the establishment and activities of this group for their support and commitment.


There is a saying deeply engraved in the collective memory of the Kurdish people: ‘We have no friends but the mountains.’ For more than a century, these words have echoed as an expression of the suffering, isolation and resistance experienced by the Kurdish people.


Throughout our history, marked by forced displacement, denial, assimilation and violence, the mountains have been more than a refuge for our people. They have been places where we preserved our identity, language, culture and hope for freedom.


The mountains became a sanctuary for our people as we fled the chemical attacks of Saddam Hussein's regime, sought protection from the executions and repression of the Iranian regime, faced Turkey's military operations or fought against the darkness of ISIS.


For many years, Kurds felt alone. They waited for the world to see them, hear their suffering and understand their just struggle.


But over time, something began to change. Friends of the Kurdish people began to emerge, raise their voices and stand shoulder to shoulder with us. You have shown us that we do have friends. The Parliamentary Friendship Group whose establishment we are celebrating here today is one of the most tangible examples of this solidarity.”


‘

The Kurdish people have friends all over the world’


Gülfer Olan, Co-Chair of the Federation of Democratic Kurdish Societies in Australia, also said that the establishment of the Kurdish Friendship Group marked an important development for the Kurdish community in Australia.


Olan said: “Achieving a historic first here today is a great source of encouragement for us as the Kurdish community. Seeing that the Kurdish people have valuable friends all over the world, beyond their mountains, gives us strength. On behalf of the Kurdish community in Australia, we extend our gratitude to everyone who contributed to this valuable initiative and hope that solidarity with the Kurdish people's struggle for freedom will continue to grow.”


DEM Party: Solidarity with the Kurdish people's democratic struggle will grow stronger


A message from the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) was read out at the event by KNK member Brusk Ayveri.


The DEM Party welcomed the establishment of the Kurdish Friendship Group in its message, stating:


“As the DEM Party, we warmly welcome the establishment of the Parliamentary Friends of the Kurdish People Group within the Australian Parliament and extend our heartfelt congratulations on this valuable initiative.


The Kurdish people are a vital and founding force in the development of democracy, peace and freedom in all four parts of Kurdistan. The Kurdish people's struggle for equality and justice is a fundamental guarantee not only of their collective rights but also of the democratisation of the regions in which they live.


We believe that this newly established friendship group will deepen dialogue and solidarity between the Australian Parliament and the democratic representatives of …

title: Jineolojî Conference: We aim to develop a perspective for the new period and overcome the challenges
content:
The first Europe-wide Jineolojî Conference has begun in Haelen, the Netherlands. More than 100 delegates from various European countries are gathering for three days of discussions on the experiences gained over ten years of organized Jineolojî activities, its role in building a democratic society, and new perspectives on organization. At the opening, Elif Kaya of the Jineolojî Academy called for a critical assessment of both the achievements made so far and the shortcomings that remain.


The conference is being held under the motto “Bi Jineolojî ber bi avakirina jiyana komunal û azad” (With Jineology towards building a communal and free life). Participants include representatives of Jineolojî committees, women’s councils and communes, mothers of fallen fighters, youth and cultural organizations, media workers, faith communities, and academics.


The gathering opened with a musical performance by artist Sosin and a minute of silence in memory of the women who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom movement. Portraits displayed in the conference hall commemorate figures including Sakine Cansız, Nagihan Akarsel, Hevrîn Xelef, and Alina Sánchez (Lêgerîn Çiya).


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261016111906_2026-10-16-haelen-avrupa-jineoloji-konferansı-hozan-sosin-1.mp4


From an idea to an organized movement in seven countries


In her opening speech, Elif Kaya reflected on the development of Jineolojî, which Abdullah Öcalan first formulated as a distinct concept in 2008. She explained that the initial discussions had evolved into a movement bringing together women from diverse social and cultural backgrounds.


“We are experiencing a historic moment. Exactly 18 years have passed since Öcalan first defined Jineolojî in 2008. Today, we are holding our first conference to evaluate Jineolojî activities across Europe,” Kaya stated.


She continued: “Every concept is like a seed; when it finds the right place and encounters favorable conditions, it grows, flourishes, and bears fruit. From the very beginning, Jineolojî, as a concept that touches upon the truth, was enthusiastically welcomed, embraced, developed, and deepened by people from different communities and social groups, particularly women, who were seeking a life in freedom.


Even before Jineolojî had established an organizational structure or developed its own framework for activities, Jineolojî conferences were held across Europe with the participation of women from different peoples and faiths. These gatherings hosted the first discussions on Jineolojî. Everyone shared the knowledge they had accumulated with others and, in turn, gained something from what others shared.


Words were not the only means of expression here; emotions, art, and body language also spoke. History spoke, culture spoke. In those moments when women shared their knowledge, we saw that language is not limited to words and that there are many ways to understand one another. Above all, Jineolojî enabled us to gain knowledge about our own existence and deepen our understanding of the meaning behind our practices and experiences.”


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261016111518_2026-10-16-haelen-avrupa-jineoloji-konferansı-elif-kaya-1.mp4


‘Jineolojî


has developed into an organized movement in seven countries’


Elif Kaya stated that Jineolojî activities have reached a significant level across Europe, is now organized in seven countries and has paved the way for new initiatives in many others. These activities have laid the groundwork for organization in various other fields, Kaya said and continued:


“Jineolojî activities in Europe, which began with a single concept, have now developed into an organized movement operating in seven European countries and laying the groundwork for Jineolojî initiatives in many others. Numerous new areas of organization that emerged in subsequent years drew their initial inspiration from Jineolojî.


Thousands of people who had questions, challenged their existing way of life, and sought alternative ways of living received education, while research activities were also carried out.


Undoubtedly, 18 years is a short period for the development of a science. Yet, looking back, it is also a considerable length of time. This period was marked by tremendous efforts and sacrifices.”

title: TMMOB Meteoroloji Mühendisleri Odası: "Selin nedeni yağışlar değil, rant odaklı kentleşme"
content:
TMMOB Meteoroloji Mühendisleri Odası, İstanbul'da yaşanan sel felaketine ilişkin yazılı açıklama yaptı. Açıklamada, felaketin nedeninin yağışlar değil, yapılaşma ve rant odaklı kentleşme politikaları olduğu belirtildi.

Oda, "Bu felaketlerin nedeni doğa değil, kentlerin rant uğruna kent ruhundan uzak bir anlayışla inşa edilmesidir" ifadelerini kullanarak yetkili kurumların sorumluluğu yağışlara yüklediğini belirtti.

Açıklamada, basında yer alan "Son 84 yılın en şiddetli yağışı" ve "Üç ayda yağması gereken yağış bir günde yağdı" ifadelerinin bilimsel olmadığı vurgulandı. İstanbul'da geçmiş yıllarda da yüksek yağış değerlerinin görüldüğü hatırlatılarak son yağışların meteorolojik açıdan beklenebilecek kuvvetli yağışlar olduğu ifade edildi.

Her afetin iklim değişikliğine bağlanmasının yanıltıcı olduğu belirtilen açıklamada, yanlış imar çalışmalarının; iklim değişikliği söylemiyle örtülmeye çalışıldığı savunuldu. Kasım ayında Antalya'da düzenlenecek COP31 toplantısında da bu konunun gündeme getirileceği belirtildi.

Oda, geçmişte su baskını yaşanmayan eski yapıların bugün sular altında kalmasının nedeninin yeni yapılaşmalar olduğunu belirtti. Bilimsel temelden yoksun yapılaşmaların suyun doğal akışını değiştirdiği, mevcut dere yataklarını olumsuz etkileyerek başka bölgelerde su baskınlarına yol açtığı ifade edildi.

Açıklamada, afetlerin ardından gündeme getirilen dere ıslahı ve yeni kent projelerinin sorunu çözmek yerine yeni maliyetler ve müteahhitlik işleri yarattığı savunuldu.

Meslek odaları ve bilim insanlarının yıllardır uyarılarda bulunduğu hatırlatılan açıklamada, 1943 yılında çıkarılan 4373 sayılı Taşkın Sulara ve Su Baskınlarına Karşı Korunma Kanunu'nun uygulanması gerektiği belirtildi.

Oda, "Çözüm, dereleri betonla kapatmak değil, onları serbest bırakmaktır" diyerek kent planlamasında meteorolojik verilerin, jeolojik koşulların, toprak özelliklerinin ve topografik yapının dikkate alınması çağrısında bulundu.

Açıklama şu ifadelerle sonlandırıldı:

"Yağışlar suçlu değildir. Asıl sorumluluk, bilimsel verileri dikkate almayan yanlış kentleşme, rant odaklı planlama ve uygulanmayan mevzuattadır. Kimse sorumluluğu doğaya yükleyerek kendini aklamasın. Kentlerimizi meteorolojik ve jeolojik gerçeklere uygun hale getirmek mümkündür. Yeter ki bilime ve hukuka dayalı kamucu planlama anlayışı hayata geçirilsin."

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Ji CHPyê 48 kes hatin îxraçkirin
content:
Lijneya Dîsîplînê ya Bilind (YDK) a Partiya Gel a Komarî (CHP), di civîna ku îro pêk anî de biryar da ku 48 kes ji partiyê bên derxistin.


Li gorî nûçeya TV100ê, Lijneyê ceza li Serokê Berê ê Bajarê Bedlîsê Metin Guzelkaya û Endamê Berê ê Meclîsa Partiyê (PM) Ozan Varal ne birî.


Di Tebaxê de ji bo dîsîplînê hatibûn şandin


Bi biryara tedbîrê ya ku Dadgeha Edliyeyê ya Herêma Enqereyê di 21ê Gulanê de dabû, Kemal Kiliçdaroglu erka Serokatiya Giştî ya CHPyê girtibû ser milê xwe. Ozgur Ozel û 91 parlementerên ligel wî de di 24ê Tîrmehê de ji CHPyê veqetiyabûn û Partiya Nû ava kiribûn. Hin rêveberên berê yên partiyê ku nêzî Ozel bûn jî endametiya xwe ya CHPê domandibûn.


Meclîsa Partiyê ya CHPê, di civîna xwe ya 26ê Tebaxê de bi daxwaza derxistina teqez û bi tedbîr 49 kes sewqî YDKyê kiribûn.


Di nav kesên ku hatibûn sewqkirin de Sekretera Giştî ya Berê Selin Sayek Boke, Cîgira Serokê Giştî ya Berê Gul Çiftci, Seroka Giştî ya Berê ya Baskê Jinan Aylin Nazliaka, endamên berê yên Lijneya Rêveberiya Navendî (MYK) Yalçin Karatepe, Zeliha Aksaz Şahbaz û Yankı Bagcioglu jî hebûn.


Berdevkê CHPê Muslim Sari piştî biryarê daxuyaniyek dabû û diyar kiribû ku wan derbarê kesên ku endametiya wan a partiyê berdewam dike lê ji bo partiyên din ên siyasî dixebitin de pêvajoya dîsîplînê daye dest pê kirin.


Sari anî ziman ku ew xebatên endamên CHPyê yên ji bo partiyên din ne exlakî dibînin û van çalakiyan di çarçoveya bendên dîsîplînê yên partiyê de dinirxînin.

title: Φεστιβάλ RedFest 2026, Σάββατο 17/10 στο Πάντειο Πανεπιστήμιο
content:
“Στις 17 Οκτωβρίου, στο Πάντειο Πανεπιστήμιο, θα πραγματοποιηθεί το RedFest 2026: Το πρόγραμμα του festival περιλαμβάνει συναυλίες, εκθέσεις, εργαστήρια, εκδηλώσεις και ανοιχτές συζητήσεις, και μέσω αυτών επιδιώκεται να ανοίξει τη συζήτηση γύρω από τα προβλήματα και τις αγωνίες που αφορούν την καθημερινότητά μας.”


Αναλυτικά το πρόγραμμα και η αφίσα του φεστιβάλ:


Στις 17 Οκτωβρίου, στο Πάντειο Πανεπιστήμιο, θα πραγματοποιηθεί το RedFest 2026: Το πρόγραμμα του festival περιλαμβάνει συναυλίες, εκθέσεις, εργαστήρια, εκδηλώσεις και ανοιχτές συζητήσεις, και μέσω αυτών επιδιώκεται να ανοίξει τη συζήτηση γύρω από τα προβλήματα και τις αγωνίες που αφορούν την καθημερινότητά μας.


Με κεντρικό σύνθημα «Αρνούμαστε τον κόσμο τους», το RedFest δημιουργεί έναν ανοιχτό χώρο συνάντησης, προβληματισμού, συλλογικότητας και διασκέδασης απέναντι σε μια πραγματικότητα που χαρακτηρίζεται από πολέμους, φτώχεια, εκμετάλλευση και κοινωνικές ανισότητες.


Το φεστιβάλ οργανώνεται μέσα από ανοιχτές συνελεύσεις. Η διοργάνωση ξεκίνησε από ανθρώπους που γνωρίστηκαν και έδρασαν από κοινού σε κοινωνικούς και πολιτικούς αγώνες και εκδηλώσεις. Η τελική της μορφή συνδιαμορφώθηκε με όσους και όσες ανταποκρίθηκαν στο δημόσιο κάλεσμα και συμμετείχαν στις ανοιχτές συνελεύσεις, συμβάλλοντας με τις ιδέες και τη δράση τους.


Το RedFest καλεί όσους θέλουν να συζητήσουν, να προβληματιστούν και να αναζητήσουν συλλογικούς τρόπους δράσης να συμμετάσχουν και να γίνουν μέρος αυτής της προσπάθειας.


Για εμάς, το RedFest δεν ολοκληρώνεται το βράδυ της 17ης Οκτωβρίου. Στόχος μας είναι οι συναντήσεις, οι συζητήσεις και οι συλλογικές διεργασίες που γεννήθηκαν μέσα από τη διοργάνωσή του να συνεχιστούν και μετά το φεστιβάλ.


Όσοι και όσες το οργανώνουμε, αλλά και όσοι άνθρωποι το αγκαλιάσουν, θέλουμε να συνεχίσουμε να συζητάμε και να δρούμε συλλογικά. Με κοινό παρονομαστή την ανάγκη να μη μείνουμε παρατηρητές απέναντι στις εξελίξεις, επιδιώκουμε να ανοίξουμε μια ουσιαστική συζήτηση για τους τρόπους με τους οποίους μπορούμε να οργανωθούμε απέναντι σε ένα σύστημα που γεννά πολέμους, ανισότητες και αποκλεισμούς.

title: Bessere Arbeitsbedingungen für Lieferando-Rider – und Betriebsratswahlen!
content:
Dossier


„

Trotz Corona-Krise zwingt Lieferando derzeit tausende von Fahrer*innen zu arbeiten. Die Rider arbeiten 7 Tage die Woche von Mittag bis spätabends ohne Desinfektionsmittel, ohne Schutzkleidung, ohne Schulungen, ohne menschenwürdigen Lohn. Die Ausrüstung kann wegen fehlender Hygienemittel nicht gereinigt werden. Die E-Bikes, die sie gewohnt sind, dürfen sie nicht mehr nutzen. Stattdessen sollen sie ihre privaten Fahrräder nutzen. Die Verträge sind befristet. Gewerkschafter*innen wird der Zutritt in die Betriebe verweigert. Menschen, die gegen prekäre Bedingungen kämpfen, müssen befürchten, dass ihre Verträge nicht verlängert werden. Als wäre das alles nicht schlimm genug, arbeiten sie aktiv daran Betriebsratswahlen zu sabotieren. (…) Wir fordern mit dieser Petition von Lieferando: Beschafft Desinfektionsmittel für alle Rider während der Corona-Pandemie. (…) Stoppt eure perfiden Versuche, Betriebsratswahlen zu behindern. Die Rider riskieren ihre Gesundheit für euren Profit

…“

Petition von Orry Mittenmayer an Lieferando bei change.org

 

 – siehe weitere Infos seitdem:


LWC-Konferenz der Betriebsräte von Lieferando: Kuriere werden »systematisch rausgeworfen« – und landen in den Schattenflotten dubioser Subunternehmer 


»Performance-Checks« und die Mafia: Konferenz der Betriebsräte von Lieferando: Kuriere werden »systematisch rausgeworfen« – und landen in den Schattenflotten dubioser Subunternehmer


„

»Das sind Leute, die haben 20.000 Euro bezahlt, um aus Indien herzukommen, und landen direkt in den Händen der Mafia«, erklärt Samee Ullah. Es geht um Essenslieferanten wie ihn. »Das wiederhole ich seit Jahren und nichts hat sich geändert.« An dieser Stelle bricht Ullah in Lachen aus, weil er das so unglaublich findet. Auch, dass es keinen juckt. »Das ist nicht zum Lachen, aber das kann nicht wahr sein.«


Was der Kurier am Mittwoch bei einer Konferenz mit etwa 50 Teilnehmern in Berlin umreißt, sind die ganz normalen Arbeitsbedingungen in der Branche. Viele, wenn nicht die meisten Fahrer haben keinen Arbeitsvertrag. Sie erhalten deutlich weniger als den Mindestlohn, oft schwarz auf die Hand an schummrigen Treffpunkten. So unterschlägt ihr Boss, von dem sie nur eine Whats-App-Nummer kennen, die Sozialbeiträge. Auf eigenes Risiko liefern diese Kuriere Bestellungen aus, die über die Plattformen von Uber Eats, Wolt oder Lieferando gemanagt werden. Die Plattformen machen hohe Gewinne. Für die Ausbeutung der Fahrer sind Sub-Sub-Subunternehmer zuständig.


Lieferando war eine Zeit lang die Ausnahme von der Regel. Nur hier wurden Fahrer direkt angestellt. Wenn auch ohne Tarifbindung. Seit Ende 2024 setzt nun aber auch Lieferando auf das lukrativere Geschäftsmodell der Konkurrenz. Von damals deutschlandweit 10.000 direkt angestellten Lieferando-Kurieren wurden bis heute 5.500 entlassen. Die meisten arbeiten jetzt für dubiose »Flottenpartner«.


Auf der Konferenz in Berlin sprechen sie von »Schattenflotte«. Es ist eine Konferenz der Betriebsräte von Lieferando. Vielleicht die letzte, heißt es immer wieder. »Vielleicht sind wir alle bald weg.« Organisiert haben sich die Kuriere als »Lieferando Workers Collective« mit Unterstützung der NGG, die auch die Konferenz mitveranstaltet.


Bei Uber und Volt seien Betriebsräte immer undenkbar geblieben, erklärt Samee Ullah. Das liege auch an der trügerischen Attraktivität von Schwarzarbeit.  (…)


»Systematisch rausgeworfen« würden die Fahrer auch wegen Krankschreibungen. Die Rede sei da von »Performance-Checks«. In Berlin habe Lieferando mittlerweile jeden zweiten direkt angestellten Kurier gekündigt. Ungefähr tausend seien noch übrig. Von »sechs- bis siebentausend«, die in der Stadt nach Ullahs Schätzung Tag für Tag unterwegs sind. (…)


Im Bundesrat wurde Ende September eine »Entschließung« angenommen, nach der ein »Direkt­anstellungsgebot für Plattformbeschäftigte im Bereich der Essenslieferdienste gesetzlich verankert« werden soll. Anlass ist die bevorstehende Umsetzung der »EU-Plattformrichtlinie« in deutsches Recht. Bis zum 2. Dezember muss der Gesetzentwurf vorliegen. Leider wird die Direktanstellung der Kuriere von der EU-Richtlinie zwar nahegelegt, aber sie kann auch ohne das umgesetzt werden. Und sowohl Bundeskanzler Merz als auch Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche wollen das für Uber und Co. lukrative Subunternehmertum schützen

…“

Artikel von Alex Reich in der jungen Welt vom 15.10.2026
