author: Unknown
title: PFDKê ceza li Amedsporê birî
content:
Lijneya Dîsiplînê ya Futbola Profesyonel (PFDK), biryarên xwe yên derbarê bûyerên ku di maçên hefteya 7an a Lîga Superê de qewimîbûn, eşkere kir.


PFDKê di mijarên, ji ber dirûşmên “kirêt û nexweş” ên alîgirên Gençlerbîrlîgiyê yên di maça Gençlerbîrlîgî-Amedsporê ya ku li Enqereyê hat lîstin de, kartên alîgirên ên li pişta qaleya bakûr, trîbuna rojava û vîpê biryara xwe da. PFDKê xwest hem ev kes werin astengkirin û ketina wan a maçên din bê qedexekirin.


Li gorî nûçeya Ajansa Welat PFDKê 280 hezar lîre cezayê pere li Amedsporê birî. Lijneyê ev ceza wekî “bûyerên li qadê” bi nav kir û cih neda bê ka ev bûyer çi ne. Lijneyê ji ber bûyerên di gelek maçên dawiya hefteyê de qewimîn, cezayên cûda dan tîman.


Maça Mardînspor û Bursasporê


Di Lîga 1emîn a Trendyolê de, di maça ku Bursasporê di 11ê Cotmehê de li qada xwe li dijî Mardîn 1969 Sporê lîst û 2-1 winda kir.


Alîgirên Bursasporê hema hema di seranserê maçê de dirûşmên nexweş berz kirin. Dîmenên van dirûşmên nexweş li ser platformên medyaya dîjîtal bi hezaran caran hatin parvekirin. Bi taybetî dirûşmên nexweş ên li dijî golparêzê Mardînsporê Erce Kardeşler bûn rojev.


Lê belê, PFDKê ji ber bûyerên qadê li gorî xalên 52/2 û 46/1 ên FDTyê (cezarkirina tîmê ya ji ber bûyerên qadê yên ku ji aliyê temaşevan, endamên klûbê an jî futbolvanan ve hatine kirin; avêtina madeyên biyanî bo nav qadê, ketina temaşevanan bo nav qadê, vêxistina meşaleyan hwd. vedihewîne) 140 hezar TL cezayê pereyan da.


Tevî ku dirûşmên kirêt û nexweş ên alîgirên Bursasporê yên di seranserê maçê de ji aliyê her kesê ku maç ji TVyê temaşe dikir ve hat bihîstin jî, nedana cezayekî bi vî rengî careke din nîşan da ku PFDK biryarên çiqas alîgir digire.


(AY)

author: Andrea DiP
title: Por que os estudantes voltaram às ruas? – com Gutemberg Rodrigues
content:
“Estamos na rua contra a extrema direita e, sobretudo, contra o que ela representa de retrocesso no nosso país”,  é o que afirma o vice-presidente da União Nacional dos Estudantes, Gutemberg Rodrigues, nesta entrevista para o Pauta Pública que analisa a volta de estudantes às ruas após o resultado do primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais.


Desde o dia 5 de outubro, universitários têm organizado assembleias e manifestações em apoio à reeleição de Lula em diferentes cidades brasileiras. Na conversa com Andrea Dip, Gutemberg relembra o papel histórico do movimento estudantil na resistência a retrocessos, na defesa da educação pública e na formação de novas lideranças políticas, destacando também a importância de defender direitos já conquistados.

author: anred
title: Argentina, no la entenderías: la marcha que transformó un reclamo universitario en una batalla contra el ajuste
content:
Imagen: Melina Deledicque.


La quinta Marcha Federal Universitaria desbordó su reclamo original y se convirtió en una movilización multisectorial contra el ajuste. Universidades, sindicatos y organizaciones sociales defendieron la educación pública, la soberanía, los derechos sociales y los bienes comunes. Más de 100 mil personas marcharon al Congreso pese a la represión estatal.

Por Melina Deledicque (trabajadora no docente de la Facultad de Trabajo Social de la UNLP) y Mariano Féliz (trabajador docente de la Facultad de Humanidades y Ciencias de la Educación de la UNLP), para Huella del Sur.


Cronología de una marcha que unió las luchas


Hace un mes, el movimiento universitario resolvió convocar a la quinta Marcha Federal Universitaria para el jueves 15 de octubre en la Plaza de Mayo, frente a la sede del Poder Ejecutivo.


La convocatoria respondió a la negativa del Gobierno nacional a cumplir la resolución dictada por el juez de primera instancia Martín Cormick, que ordena al Poder Ejecutivo aplicar la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario, a casi un año de su aprobación.

Según el Gobierno

, la ley no está siendo incumplida, sino que se encuentra “suspendida”. Sin embargo, el Poder Ejecutivo desoye el fallo judicial, que dispone la actualización de los salarios docentes y Nodocentes y de las becas estudiantiles conforme a lo establecido por la ley.


Imagen: Melina Deledicque.


Imagen: Melina Deledicque.


Mientras tanto, el proyecto de Presupuesto 2027 contempla partidas aproximadamente un 33% inferiores a

las solicitadas

 por el Consejo Interuniversitario Nacional (CIN): mientras el Gobierno prevé unos 7,3 billones de pesos para las universidades nacionales, el CIN reclama 11 billones.


El miércoles 14 de octubre, el juez Cormick hizo efectivo el apercibimiento que había dispuesto previamente y fijó astreintes —multas compulsivas— de 100.000 pesos diarios para Diego Santilli, titular de la Jefatura de Gabinete, mientras persista el incumplimiento de la resolución judicial. La sanción recae inicialmente sobre Santilli y podría extenderse a otros funcionarios o incrementarse si el Gobierno no acata la decisión. Sin embargo, el mismo día de la movilización, la Cámara de Apelaciones puso en suspenso la multa.


Imagen: Melina Deledicque.


Imagen: Melina Deledicque.


Todo cambió con la resolución de la Corte Suprema de habilitar el artículo 154 del DNU 70/23, permitiendo la extranjerización sin límites de tierras rurales en Argentina. Si bien, frente al repudio popular, la Corte

dio marcha atrás

, el clima político ya se había enrarecido.


Estas circunstancias aceleraron la convocatoria de la oposición en la Cámara de Diputados para avanzar en el rechazo definitivo del DNU 70/23. En esa misma sesión se proponía discutir también la prórroga de la Ley de Emergencia en Discapacidad y una ley destinada a aliviar la situación de las familias sobreendeudadas y en mora.


Recordemos que el Senado de la Nación ya había votado la derogación del DNU 70/23 a comienzos de 2024. Ese decreto continúa en el centro de la escena por sus efectos sobre el precio de los alquileres, las tasas de interés de los créditos y las cuotas de la medicina prepaga, entre otros aspectos. En la Cámara de Diputados, la oposición nunca consiguió los votos necesarios para avanzar en ese sentido. Lamentablemente, este jueves tampoco se alcanzó el quórum para habilitar la sesión.

Varios gobernadores

 aliados del gobierno libertariano blindaron el DNU 70/23, ya que diputados de Tucumán, Jujuy y Santa Fe vaciaron sus bancas, al igual que los gobernadores de Unión por la Patria, Melella y Zamora.


Imagen: Melina Deledicque.


Imagen: Melina Deledicque.


Con ese contexto, la comunidad universitaria decidió que la movilización sería frente al Congreso. De esa manera, en pocas semanas, una marcha inicialmente convocada por el movimiento universitario se transformó en una movilización multisectorial de alcance nacional, con concentraciones frente al Congreso y en las principales plazas de todo el país.


La movilización sumó más de 100 mil personas en CABA (y decenas de miles más en el resto del país)

, y se sostuvo a pesar de un clima inhóspito e incluso un chaparrón intenso al cierre. A la misma se sumaron

organizaciones de personas con discapacidad, de familias endeudadas, sindicatos combativos —como los integrantes del FreSU, bancarios, aceiteros, camioneros y otros—, e incluso la CGT

.


Como tantas veces, ante el reclamo legítimo …

author: groundxero
title: No Bonus, Unpaid Wages, Missing PF Dues: Thousands of Tea Workers Take to the Streets in North Bengal
content:
More than a hundred tea estates in North Bengal reportedly missed the 5 October deadline for payment of the 20% annual bonus. Thousands of workers across Merico-Sammelan gardens in the Dooars are protesting unpaid bonuses, outstanding wages and provident fund dues, even as the state government’s assurances and meetings yield little.


 


Groundxero

 | 16 October 2026


 


On the morning of Shashthi, as people across Kolkata throng Durga Puja pandals, women tea garden workers in North Bengal are taking to the streets to fight for a bonus that should already have been in their bank accounts. Workers, led by women workers from Hantapara, Gayerdanga and Dumkipara tea estates marched towards Madarihat to demand payment of their bonus. Workers at Birpara are preparing similar protests, while others staged demonstrations outside factory gates and approached the police.


 


Their immediate demand is straightforward: payment of the full 20% annual bonus. But the protests expose a much wider crisis of unpaid wages, withheld provident fund contributions, unpaid gratuity, and the continuing impunity enjoyed by tea garden owners.


 


At the centre of the current confrontation is the Merico Agro Industries and Sammelan Tea & Beverages group, which controls 12–13 tea estates employing nearly 10,000 workers, the vast majority of them women. The management has sought to persuade workers to accept a bonus of just 10%. The workers, led by the Paschim Banga Cha Majdur Samiti (PBCMS), have refused to settle for half of what they are demanding.


 


The West Bengal government had set 5 October as the deadline for payment of a 20% bonus to tea garden workers. Yet, according to available reports, only 170 of the Dooars’ 285 tea gardens had paid bonuses by 10 October. More than a hundred estates had reportedly failed to pay workers even a single rupee.


 


The failure is particularly revealing because the change of government in West Bengal was accompanied by the BJP’s promise of a new political and administrative dispensation. For tea garden workers, however, the much-publicised ‘double engine’ government appears to be running along the same tracks as its predecessor: false assurances for workers, impunity for defaulting employers, and little effective action to compel payment.


 


Last year, the Trinamool Congress government had also advised employers to pay a 20% bonus. This year, the BJP government issued a similar directive, setting a deadline of 5 October. But an advisory, however emphatically worded, is no substitute for enforcement. Employers continue to delay and withheld payments while workers lose wages, spend days in demonstrations and struggle to meet their basic needs.


 


Pay slips issued but no payment made


 


The confrontation at Bagrakote Tea Garden illustrates the gap between management promises and workers’ actual experience. After the bonus remained unpaid, workers went on strike and blocked the Siliguri–Dooars national highway at Meena More. Following the mobilisation, the management issued a notice promising payment of the 20% bonus by 13–14 October.


 


Both dates passed without the promised payment.


 


On the night of 14 October, owner Surajit Bakshi telephoned PBCMS leaders and reportedly asked them to persuade workers to accept a 10% bonus, saying that this was all he had managed to arrange. The union refused to endorse the proposal, maintaining the workers’ demand for the full bonus.


 


On 15 October, garden managers distributed pay slips promising a 20% bonus. Workers waited for the money to arrive in their bank accounts. Managers waited for funds to become available. Police stood guard over the managers, while rumours circulated among workers that payments had been made in neighbouring areas.


 


By 10 pm, according to PBCMS, not one of the approximately 10,000 workers employed across the Merico-Sammelan group’s gardens had received any money.


 


The episode captures the absurdity of a system in which paperwork and promises can be produced on schedule, but the payment of workers’ dues remains indefinitely negotiable. The workers are expected to trust pay slips, wait through successive deadlines and accept management’s financial difficulties as an excuse. Their own financial difficulties, and their rightful dues, meanwhile, receive little consideration.


 


Labour department calls meetings without accountability


 


The labour department’s handling of the dispute has added to …

author: Richard Sears
title: Four New Studies Raise Concerns About Benzodiazepine-Related Harms
content:
T

his week,

Mad in America

 examines four new studies around harms linked to benzodiazepine use. The first finds that benzodiazepines are linked to increased risk of heart failure and heart failure related hospitalization. The second reports that long-term benzodiazepine use (60 days or longer) is associated with worse cognitive function in people diagnosed with schizophrenia. The third finds that taking these drugs during pregnancy is linked to an increased risk of miscarriage. The fourth links benzodiazepines to increased risk of falls and fractures in older adults.


Benzodiazepines Linked to Increased Risk of Heart Failure


A new

study

 published in

Cardiovascular Toxicology

 finds that benzodiazepine use is linked to higher risk of heart failure and heart failure related hospitalization in people prescribed these drugs to treat insomnia. This research, led by Yi-Sin Huang from Taipei Medical University in Taiwan, also suggests that benzodiazepines are associated with a higher risk of heart failure hospitalization than other drugs used to treat insomnia.


The goal of this study was to examine the link between heart failure and benzodiapepine use in people with insomnia. The authors also wanted to compare heart failure outcomes between benzodiapepines and other drugs prescribed for insomnia. They conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of previous research on this topic. In total, they used data from 11 studies.


Benzodiazepine use was linked to a 41% increased risk of heart failure and a 29% increased risk of heart failure related hospitalization compared to non-use. The risk of heart failure related hospitalizations in people taking these drugs to treat insomnia was also elevated compared to other drugs, including Z-drugs, suvorexant,and antipsychotics. These increased risks were particularly elevated in people that had a history of heart failure and those at high-risk.


This research had three main limitations. Most of the included studies were observational, meaning the findings can speak to a link between bezodiazepines and heart failure, but cannot definitively say that these drugs cause heart failure. Only 11 studies were included in the current work. The included studies varied significantly in follow-up range, methods, and patient populations.


Benzodiazepines Linked to Worse Cognitive Functioning


A new

study

 published in

BMC Psychiatry

 finds that long-term benzodiazepine use is linked to worse cognitive functioning in people diagnosed with schizophrenia. This research, led by Caiping Liu from the Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine in China, also reports that there was no significant difference in terms of cognition between low- and high-dose users. This means that while any long-term benzodiazepine use was associated with poorer cognition, the current work did not find that higher doses were linked to poorer cognitive function.


The authors used data from the SALT-C study in China, a research project around atypical antipsychotic use in people diagnosed with schizophrenia. They used data collected from 114 SALT-C participants recruited at the Shanghai Mental Health Center between 2016 and 2019. For the purposes of analysis the authors divided participants into two groups, people that had never taken benzodiazepines before and those that had taken a stable dose for at least 60 consecutive days. Each of these groups included 57 participants. The groups were similar in terms of sex, age, duration of illness, and types of atypical antipsychochotics prescribed. There were also no significant differences in overall psychiatric symptoms severity, “illness” severity, or psychological functioning.


Long-term benzodiazepine users had an average score of 16.02 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment compared to 19.33 for non-users. This indicated significantly poorer cognitive performance for participants taking benzodiazepines for at least 60 consecutive days. This deficit was observed mostly in the visuospatial and executive cognitive domain, meaning benzodiazepine users had greater difficulty understanding visual/spatial information and planning, organizing, and solving problems. The authors note that there was no clear dose-response relationship between benzodiazepine use and cognitive impairment. This means similar cognitive impairment was observed in both low- and high-dose users.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Marcos Congress set to pass another corrupt budget, progressives warn
content:
Progressive legislators expressed alarm over the 2027 national budget passed by the House of Representatives (HOR) on Monday, saying it is the opposite of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s promise of cleaner government spending.


“The Marcos budget they are passing is not a budget for Filipinos. It only funds politicians, political dynasties and war and militarism against our people,” the Makabayan Coalition lawmakers said in voting against the measure.


The HOR approved a P7.2-trillion budget for next year, the biggest in the country’s history. With a few alterations to accommodate pet projects of Marcos allies in the chamber, the total amount followed the national expenditure program earlier submitted by Marcos.


How did the budget pass so quickly?


Marcos allies control the HOR. Led by a Speaker loyal to the president and persuaded by the Senior Deputy Speaker who happens to be Marcos’ eldest son Sandro, 282 legislators agreed to the proposed budget.


Only 13 voted against the proposal while a lone representative abstained.


The HOR glowingly described the approved budget as a

 “

boost to public education and health, as well as the country’s preparations for El Niño” now starting to affect the Southeast Asian country.


Opponents of the measure, however, said Marcos’ budget is meant to continue both patronage politics and corruption the Philippine government is notorious for.


Who opposed Marcos’ planned budget?


Of the 254 district representatives of the Philippines Congress – as many as 80 per cent of whom are members of political dynasties – only five voted against the measure. Eight of their fellow oppositionists are party representatives, led by the three members of the progressive Makabayan Coalition.


The few HOR members who opposed the “porky” 2027 proposed General Appropriations Act. (HOR photo)


ACT Teachers Representative Antonio Tinio pointed out that while the Marcos proposal already reduced the budget for public health, the president’s allies further reduced Department of Health’s budget. He said funds on health facilities and equipment, commodities for family health, immunization, nutrition and responsible parenting, Health Promotion and Quick Response Fund would be reduced by billions of pesos.


Tinio also revealed that funds for education would be substantially cut, impacting construction and renovation of classrooms as well as the country’s school computerization program


Contrary to government claims the budget factors in effects of the El Niño, government’s calamity fund was also reduced by P9.5 billion, Tinio revealed.


What does the Marcos budget contain?


 

Appropriations Committee chairperson and Representative Mikaela Angela Suansing was in tears when the HOR approved the budget on Monday night, overjoyed by the approval of the proposal she pushed along for months.


“The House’s budget amendments were guided by the shared judgment of the House to protect key spending priorities, particularly education and healthcare, while responding to the most pressing needs of the Filipino people,” she claimed.


Leaders of the House of Representatives celebrate after passing its version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill. (HOR photo)


Kabataan Youth Represenative Renee Louise Co, however, disagreed with Suansing’s glowing description of their work.


“Mister Speaker, this begs the question: What is taking up all that fiscal space? Year-in, year-out, the national budget is overflowing with pork [barrel],” Co exclaimed in her explanation of her rejection of the proposed budget.


Co revealed that the approved budget retained P361.19 billion for the Marcos government’s controversial infrastructure projects, such flood control and farm-to-market roads.


The budget would also give P136.94 billion to Marcos’ financial assistance programs the young legislator said are used to deodorize the president’s failure to defend the economy against uncertainties brought by the conflicts in West Asia.


Co also flagged the P51.88 billion that would be given to Marcos as “discretionary funds.”


Can the budget still be cleaned?


While the HOR holds the Philippine government’s “power of the purse,” the proposed 2027 budget has yet to go through the Philippine Senate before it is signed into law.


Tinio said he hopes that instead of introducing pork barrel-type amendments of its own, the Senate should make the necessary corrections by decreasing allotted funds for congressmen’s pet projects and …

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Councils Face Upheaval After Labour Threat to End Coalitions With Greens
content:
Labour’s threat to end local power-sharing agreements with the Greens in response to its ‘Zionism is racism’ motion could lead to disruption at councils across England and Wales. 


Bridget Phillipson, Labour’s chair, said on Thursday that Greens working in coalition with the party in local councils must “make clear that they reject” the motion. Otherwise, she said, “Labour will bring any such local arrangement to an end”.  


She also echoed a claim by prime minister Andy Burnham that the motion is “antisemitic”. In response, the Greens accused Labour of conflating criticism of Israel with antisemitism.


Between 17 and 19 councils could be affected if Labour ends the agreements, according to various media reports. They include Sheffield City Council, which is at “risk of collapse” if Labour ends their coalition with the Greens, the

Yorkshire Post reported

. 


Wealden Council, which is led by Green party deputy leader Rachel Millward, may also be affected. The council is dominated by the Greens and Lib Dems, with Labour providing two councillors to give the alliance a slender majority. Before Labour joined, the alliance led the council without a majority. 


Millward has already publicly opposed the motion. Green leader Zack Polanski did not vote and has said he wanted amendments, including one aimed at reassuring people within the party who attend Zionist synagogues. Members, not leaders, passed

the motion

 by 1,022 votes to 813 at their annual conference on 4 October.


The motion says Zionism calls for “an ethnonationalist Jewish state” and has led to the “dehumanisation, displacement, dispossession, disenfranchisement and destruction of Palestinians” while creating “racial hierarchies”. 


A Green party spokesperson said in a statement: “For the Labour government to conflate criticism of Israel with antisemitism is disappointing and wrong. Trying to tell local parties what to do and who they can work with is undemocratic. Whilst Labour continue to try to meddle in our internal democracy, arm a genocide and lock up protesting pensioners, we will not take lectures from them.” 


Speaking during prime minister’s questions on Wednesday, Burnham ruled out a national coalition with the Greens because of the motion. 


Polanski

hit back at Burnham’s statement

 on X. “I’m the only Jewish leader of a political party. I’m a victim of antisemitism every day and I’ve made it clear Jewish people are welcome in my party,” he wrote. “You’re a prime minister who arms a genocide and locks pensioners up for opposing it.


“A Labour government who apologised over their actions over Gaza is demonstrating that it was all performative. Andy Burnham still stands with Israel whilst it kills innocent people,” he said.

title: Llamamiento de la Mesa Sindical de Madrid a la construcción de Comités Unitarios para la Huelga General del 11N
content:
Para construir la huelga general desde abajo:


Impulsemos comités unitarios por la huelga general en todos los centros de trabajo, centros de estudio, barrios y pueblos de Madrid.


Esta huelga general

nace de la lucha y la exigencia popular en las plazas y en las calles

, que ha logrado que todas las organizaciones sindicales se sumaran a la convocatoria.


Desde la

Mesa Sindical por la huelga general

 hemos entendido desde el inicio que las garantías de éxito del 11N y de continuidad de esta lucha es que seamos capaces de

organizarla desde abajo, en cada centro de trabajo, en cada centro de estudio, en cada barrio y pueblo

. Esto exige la articulación consciente, democrática y solidaria de comités unitarios por la huelga general.


Por ello,

hacemos un llamamiento a todas las organizaciones sindicales, sociales, juveniles, políticas y a todo el activismo

 a la conformación masiva de comités unitarios, en la que,

de forma democrática y asamblearia, construyamos espacios de debate y organización no excluyentes y con capacidad de tomar decisiones colectivas

.


Son ya muchas las iniciativas que se están poniendo en marcha.

Saludamos ese empeño y esperamos y deseamos que ese espíritu unitario, participativo y democrático prevalezca en todas partes

.


¡Organicemos una gran huelga general activa y combativa el 11-N! ¡Continuemos la lucha y la organización después del 11N, gobierne quien gobierne!

author: CNT Iruña
title: Sorpresa sería que aguantáramos
content:
Cada vez que sale una estadística sobre bajas, la misma historia. Que si faltamos mucho, que si el estrés y la ansiedad se disparan, que la gente ya no aguanta nada. Y ni una vez se preguntan por qué. Pues lo decimos nosotras, que lo tenemos claro: es que nos han dejado a media plantilla y nos piden el trabajo de una y media. Es que te escriben a las diez de la noche y más te vale contestar. Es que los objetivos están puestos para que no los cumpla nadie. Es que con estos contratos no llegas a fin de mes, y encima vives con el miedo al despido pegado al cuerpo, todo el día, hasta cuando duermes. Así que no me digas que es sorpresa. Sorpresa sería que aguantáramos.


Y cuando por fin alguien se cae, la empresa se encoge de hombros y le cuelga el cartel de absentista, como si fuera un defecto de fábrica. Años culpando al que enferma para no tener que mirar lo que enferma. Ya está bien, ¿no?


Una baja por salud mental no es un capricho, por mucho que lo piense algún jefe. Y algún compañero, que también los hay, no nos vamos a engañar. Es parar antes de romperte del todo. Y tienes todo el derecho a hacerlo sin pedir perdón a nadie. No somos máquinas. Nuestra vida vale más que los beneficios de cuatro. La salud no se regatea ni se agradece como si fuera un favor personal del jefe de turno. Es un derecho que costó décadas de lucha, y no vamos a dejar que nos lo vayan recortando por la puerta de atrás. Si media plantilla acaba quemada, el problema no son las personas. Es una empresa que te gasta y te tira, como si fueras material fungible.


Así que sí, cuidarse también es político. El que se coge la baja no le falla a nadie. Y la culpa, esa que te meten, sirve para una cosa: para que te calles. Pues va a ser que no.


¿Y ahora qué? Pues lo de siempre, lo que ha funcionado toda la vida. Cubrirnos entre compañeras cuando una no puede más. No dejar sola a la que se cae. Cortar el cotilleo de quién está de baja y por qué, que bastante tiene ya. Y plantarnos juntas en el curro para exigir plantillas completas, ritmos que aguante un ser humano y desconexión de verdad, no la del convenio que nadie respeta. Derechos laborales no nos han regalado ninguno. Todos se han arrancado peleando. Este también.

author: Unknown
title: Torino: incursioni della polizia dentro le scuole occupate
content:
Di seguito il comunicato pubblicato dall’

Assemblea Studentesca

 delle scuole di Torino in merito ai fatti degli ultimi giorni.


La quasi totalità delle scuole torinesi è in occupazione a partire dalla settimana scorsa con l’intento di scendere in piazza tutte unite. Licei e istituti tecnici da giorni sono l’epicentro della lotta studentesca contro la riforma Valditara, il razzismo istituzionale, la guerra, la spesa per le armi, per chiedere urgenti fondi per ristrutturare le nostre scuole, contro le scuole trasformate in caserme e lo strapotere dei presidi.


In migliaia stiamo affermando i nostri diritti e soprattutto che vogliamo contare! Che come studenti e studentesse vogliamo potere decisionale sulle nostre vite e sulle nostre scuole.


Il Governo Meloni e il Prefetto di Torino ci attaccano senza rispondere alle nostre rivendicazioni, cercando di dividerci tra “buoni e cattivi”. Minacciano di intervenire contro le occupazioni e i nostri cortei. Rispondiamo che siamo uniti più che mai è che la nostra lotta è compatta! 


La lotta studentesca in maniera spontanea ha assunto anche forme nuove. Se una parte degli studenti vede nelle strutture scolastiche un obiettivo da colpire la colpa è di chi le ha fatte diventare delle caserme, di chi le ha rese fatiscenti, di chi le ha definanziate per anni, di chi ha fatto finta di non vedere che il razzismo istituzionale era sempre più forte. 


Invece di chiedersi perché alcuni studenti arrivino ad odiare le proprie scuole, i propri banchi, i propri professori, ci si inventa fantomatici “infiltrati” a cui dare la colpa. Si guarda il dito e non la luna. Noi invece siamo consapevoli che dietro a questi comportamenti spontanei c’è la voglia di contare, di farsi sentire, di urlare che esistiamo. Dirigenti scolastici, professori, Prefetto e Ministro dovrebbero chiedersi perché, invece di invocare manette e strette repressive. 


Il nostro movimento è fatto di rifiuto e contrapposizione, ma in questi giorni di vita comune e occupazione, sta generando proposte concrete per una scuola diversa da quella che il sistema ci obbliga a vivere. Laboratori, assemblee, dibattiti sono la fucina in cui un mondo che vogliamo nuovo e collettivo sta nascendo, questo è quello che fa più paura al potere, scoprire che chi si pensava passivo e alienato invece ha vita, idee, voglia di mettersi in gioco. 


Dalla Francia gli studenti ci hanno invitato a muoverci insieme e lo abbiamo fatto, scoprendo che la nostra città può essere un esempio per tante altre in Italia. Molti giornalisti benpensanti nelle settimane scorse guardavano  raccontavano con ammirazione le mobilitazioni al di là del confine, ora che sono arrivate a casa loro e le hanno sotto il naso le oscurano e le criminalizzano. La rivolta per loro va bene solo se la fanno in altri paesi per poi dirci che noi non siamo maturi, che qui è diverso. Bene, ora che la prateria si è incendiata anche qui dovranno farsene una ragione. 


Alle minacce del Prefetto contro le occupazioni  rispondiamo compatti che le difenderemo, a testimoniarlo ci sono le montagne di banchi e cassonetti che sbarrano gli ingressi. Diciamo che gli arresti di oggi contro gli studenti del Levi e di Giaveno sono assurdi e criminali.


I presidi ci parlano di “esterni” come se le nostre occupazioni fossero fatte da infiltrati. Questi fantomatici “esterni” non sono altro che studenti e studentesse che da scuola a scuola si danno man forte a vicenda, creano legami e solidarietà. Chi ha deciso che non possiamo confrontarci fra scuole diverse? Forse si arrabbiano tanto perché per una volta la scuola è aperta a chi decidiamo noi e non loro, è la frustrazione di chi vede il proprio potere vacillare.

author: CNT Santander
title: Ni alquileres abusivos, ni sueldos de miseria
content:
La huelga es la mejor herramienta que tiene la clase trabajadora para conquistar derechos al sistema capitalista. Las mejoras laborales, las libertades y los avances sociales son fruto de la organización, la solidaridad y la lucha colectiva. Cuando nos unimos, tenemos la capacidad de detener la maquinaria que se alimenta de nuestro esfuerzo.


Desde CNT Santander nos unimos a la llamada del Sindicato de Inquilinas y el 11 de noviembre saldremos a la calle para reivindicar nuestros derechos como clase trabajadora.


Es por todo ello que:


Revindicamos un

incremento salarial

 en todos los sectores, incluido el salario mínimo interprofesional, que nos permita poder asumir los costes de la vida sin sentir que nos ahogamos, sin incertidumbre ni pánico.


Necesitamos la

reducción de la jornada laboral máxima

 a 30 horas semanales, sin merma salarial, de manera progresiva.


Lucharemos por

un incremento de las pensiones públicas

, tanto contributivas como no contributivas.


La vivienda no es un lujo para especular, es un derecho innegociable que ha de ser respetado. Ninguna persona debería elegir entre pagar el alquiler, llenar la nevera y/o encender la calefacción este invierno. Ninguna familia debería vivir con miedo a perder su hogar mientras existen viviendas convertidas en mercancía para la especulación de los fondos buitre.


Exigimos una vivienda digna y asequible para todas las personas

, que se intervengan y regulen los precios, que no haya que destinar más del 30% a este fin, necesitamos que se ponga un límite a los alquileres abusivos que desestabilizan las economías familiares, la

protección social frente a los desahucios

 y unas

medidas directas y efectivas

 que pongan las necesidades humanas por delante del beneficio privado, sobre todo las de las personas más vulnerables.


Reclamamos una

estabilidad en el empleo

 para no vivir con inseguridad, para poder tener planes de futuro y también una

estabilidad en el arrendamiento de la vivienda

. Precisamos

contratos de alquiler indefinidos

, no interrumpidos con la llegada del turismo masivo y acabar con la expulsión temporal.


¡A LA HUELGA GENERAL!

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: 2023 Operation Al-Aqsa Flood as resistance vs US-Israel
content:
“We cannot condemn the genocide in Palestine without also condemning the imperialist United States.”

Filipino activists remembered the Operation Al-Aqsa Flood three years ago as the day Palestinians amplified their stand against imperialism.

Led by the International League of Peoples’ Struggle (ILPS) Philippines, Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association (PPFA), and the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan), activists marched on October 7 to the US Embassy to remember the historic operation against Israeli occupation after decades of Palestinian oppression.

Carrying the Palestinian flag and placards with images of slain journalists in Gaza, they marched along Kalaw Avenue in Ermita, Manila to condemn the Israeli attacks despite the ceasefire that supposedly took effect on October 10, 2025.

During the program, Amirah Lidasan, secretary-general of Moro Christian People’s Alliance and co-chairperson of Sandugo Movement of Moro and Indigenous Peoples for Self-Determination, said, “Gaza is not the land of another people. Gaza belongs to the Palestinians who are struggling.”

In 2025, US President Donald Trump introduced the Gaza peace plan, also known as the “Board of Peace,” which saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza. It also includes an agreement to end the war.

According to the Palestinian Ministry of Health, Israeli attacks since the October 7, 2023 Operation Al-Aqsa Flood have killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, including at least 21,000 children. The actual death toll may be higher, as official records rely on documented deaths and do not account for those still missing or buried under the rubble.

Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) Chairperson and former Bayan Muna Rep. Teddy Casiño highlighted the US role in Israel’s attacks on Palestine by continuing to provide unconditional financial and military support

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) rely heavily on imported arms from the US which accounts for 69 percent of Israel’s weapon imports from 2019-2023.

“We cannot condemn the genocide in Palestine without also condemning the imperialist United States. Not only has Israel committed genocide in Palestine, but the United States has also attached Venezuela, Iran and Yemen, and is now there is possibility to attack Cuba,” Casiño said.

On January 3, the United States abducted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his spouse, Cilia Flores, following months of US strikes in the Caribbean and Pacific that reportedly killed more than 100 people.

The Trump administration’s actions, which critics have condemned as violations of international law and Venezuela’s national sovereignty, reflect what the progressive groups describe as a longstanding pattern of US imperialism.

Despite the controversy surrounding the operation, the Trump administration insisted on its intention to “run the country,” further raising concerns over Venezuela’s sovereignty and the Venezuelan people’s right to self-determination.

Rev. Alan Sarte, secretary-general of the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association stressed the determination of Palestinians to continue fighting for their freedom, calling on people around the world to oppose imperialism and defend national sovereignty.

author: Oyunga Pala
title: When Baba Died: One Year Later
content:
Last October, two weeks before Baba died, I was returning to Nairobi after a two-year hiatus. The last time I was home was during the first-year memorial of my sister, Nyangi, who was now the prominent character in my book.


Home had changed in many ways, yet it had not, in a kind of same old but different way. The vibe was familiar, the actors younger, the pace faster. Roads once familiar were now dwarfed by high-rise towers sprouting around the city like wild mushrooms. The expressway from the airport straddling the city dominated the cityscape, a marker of a city in a hurry to grow up.


I used to wonder whether I would change. Would I be like the other diaspora Kenyans I had seen who lost all sense of belonging after just a few miserable winters abroad, and began to look down on their own? Stepping away seemed to have had the opposite effect on me.


This notion of belonging was immediately tested as I faced my former public self. When I announced that I had published a book and would be going on a book tour, the reception was warm. I was reminded of how big

Mantalk

 was, the weekly national column in the Daily Nation that I laboured over for a decade and that has now become part of the country’s cultural landscape, a reference point to a bygone era, for many stuck in nostalgia. I was no longer the Mantalk guy. I had traveled far both within and without. I had grown up, but to many of my readers, I was still that guy, who showed up every Saturday, a mysterious figure who ruffled feathers. The man some female readers used to love to hate.


I had been part of several life journeys unwittingly. And like all fans of urban culture, I was a mascot for those bygone times. Yet here I was, older, perhaps wiser, certainly a lot humbler. I had just poured my soul into a book that detailed my own journey away from the glam and fame of the national spotlight and delved into trying not only to make sense of my unresolved grief but also the grief of a nation. The shift in persona was stark: From a young man who used to critique modern rules of chivalry to one sharing lessons on how to navigate the profound loss that follows the death of a loved one.


To reach these moments of connection, I first had to navigate the city itself. My first stop the night after my arrival was the Prestige Bookshop and Nairobi traffic- well, what has changed? The roads remained clogged, and nothing quite captures Nairobi’s class dynamics as the expressway, raised above, smooth and scenic, with arresting views of flashy high-rise buildings obscuring the reality of chaos that rules just underneath it, bottleneck traffic, matatu madness, and boda bodas that now make matatus appear quite tame. It became a metaphor in hindsight of how we process grief: stoic and contained on the surface, but underneath the facade, a bubbling volcano waiting to erupt.


I remember Prestige bookshop from another time, when the city centre was a little more serene, and Mama Ngina Street still had a taste of the bourgie back when 20th Century Plaza, the Hilton hotel and the International Life House were iconic landmarks in the city centre. Yvonne Adhiambo Owuor was launching her second novel, The DragonFly Sea, in the small bookshop. The shelves had been pushed to the side to create space for the fans, and I was the MC of the day, here to celebrate one of Kenya’s finest novelists. I looked at the bookshop now, wondering how we had pulled it off, for there seemed to be hardly any room to swing a cat.


When the people started to come through, I knew this was going to be special. Odd that despite 28 years of a public writing life, I had never signed an autograph. I remained struck that people would endure Nairobi traffic to meet over a book and demand my bad handwriting on their personal copies.


I didn’t know what to expect as a new world and role began to unfold for me. Lost connections revived. People I had gone to school with, names I hadn’t seen or heard from in years. Friends, family, acquaintances, total strangers, with entwined pasts and reminders of a time once spent in communion; between the firm handshakes and tight embraces, it took me a minute to realise what was happening.


I was being honoured and celebrated. When I went to Ukombozi Library to donate a copy of my book, I met Ogutu, who told me how the story of my father’s funeral process was also his story. At the United Kenya Club, I met Clifford Derrick, who had just buried his mother, and the book …

title: Αντιφασιστική διαδήλωση στο Περιστέρι, Παρασκευή 16/10, στις 19:00
content:
Αφίσες/Καλέσματα:


Προλεταριακό Αντιφασιστικό Μέτωπο Δυτικών Προαστίων


ΑΝΤΙΦΑΣΙΣΤΙΚΗ ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΗ


ΠΑΡΑΣΚΕΥΗ 16 ΟΚΤΩΒΡΗ στις 19:00 πλατεία δημαρχείου (μετρό Περιστέρι)


ΦΑΣΙΣΤΕΣ ΤΟ ΜΕΛΛΟΝ ΣΑΣ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΠΡΟΔΙΑΓΕΓΡΑΜΜΕΝΟ


Η Δολοφονική επίθεση με μαχαίρι στον αντιφασίστα στην Ελευσίνα και η επίθεση με μπογιές και σπρέι στο στέκι της Αριστερής Κίνησης Περιστερίου θα απαντηθούν κοινωνικά και μαχητικά.


Καλούμε όλο το αντιφασιστικό κίνημα σε πλήρη συσπείρωση και μαχητική θέση ενάντια στους μαχαιροβγάλτες νοσταλγούς των ναζί.


Ο φασισμός δεν πέφτει από τον ουρανό. Γεννιέται μέσα στις αντιθέσεις της καπιταλιστικής κοινωνίας και αποτελεί την πιο ακραία και αντιδραστική μορφή υπεράσπισης της εξουσίας του κεφαλαίου. Όταν η κοινωνική οργή μεγαλώνει, ο φασισμός επιχειρεί να της δώσει άλλο στόχο. Να στρέψει τον εργαζόμενο ενάντια στον μετανάστη, τον φτωχό ενάντια στον φτωχότερο, τον έναν καταπιεσμένο ενάντια στον άλλο. Ο ρατσισμός και ο εθνικισμός είναι τα όπλα του για να διασπά την εργατική τάξη και να κρύβει τον πραγματικό ταξικό αντίπαλο.


Γινόμαστε εκ νέου μάρτυρες του ίδιου φαινομένου, σε μια εποχή πολέμων, ακρίβειας, φτώχειας και ανασφάλειας, η ακροδεξιά προσπαθεί ξανά να δηλητηριάσει την οξυμένη κοινωνική οργή με ρατσισμό, εθνικισμό και μίσος. Προσπαθεί να πείσει τον εργαζόμενο ότι για τη ζωή που του στερούν φταίει ο πρόσφυγας, ο μετανάστης, ο διαφορετικός. Να μετατρέψει την αγανάκτηση σε τυφλό μίσος και να αφήσει στο απυρόβλητο τις πραγματικές σχέσεις εκμετάλλευσης και εξουσίας.


Δεν υπάρχει πιο ειρωνική συγκυρία που να αποδεικνύει του λόγου το αληθές όταν την επόμενη της φασιστικής δολοφονικής επίθεσης στην εργατούπολη της Ελευσίνας δολοφονήθηκαν μερικά χιλιόμετρα πιο κάτω, ξανά από εργοδοτική αμέλεια, δυο εργάτες στην Motor Oil στους Αγίους Θεοδώρους. Το έγκλημα αυτό είναι ένα από τα πολλά των τελευταίων χρόνων και οι δύο εργάτες που έχασαν την ζωή τους είναι 2 από τους 142 (ΟΣΕΤΕΕ), μέχρι τώρα, εργαζομένους που έχασαν την ζωή τους εντός του 2026. Δεν είναι, λοιπόν, καθόλου τυχαίο ότι τέτοιες φασιστικές επιθέσεις πραγματοποιούνται σε ανθρώπους που μάχονται για έναν πιο δίκαιο κόσμο ή σε συλλογικότητες που επιδιώκουν να περιγράψουν μια άλλη κοινωνία χωρίς εκμετάλλευση ανθρώπου από άνθρωπο. Όπως δεν είναι τυχαίο ότι αυτά συμβαίνουν κατά βάση σε περιοχές που διαμένουν ή εργάζονται τα φτωχότερα κοινωνικά στρώματα, όπως είναι η Ελευσίνα, με βιωμένη την εργοδοτική αυθαιρεσία και την εγκληματική αμέλεια με σωρεία εργατικών ατυχημάτων και δυστυχημάτων.


Γι’ αυτό η αποφυλάκιση του Ηλία Κασιδιάρη και η δηλωμένη πρόθεσή του να επιστρέψει στην πολιτική δράση, δεν μπορούν να αντιμετωπίζονται με αδιαφορία. Η Χρυσή Αυγή δεν ήταν απλώς ένα ακροδεξιό κόμμα. Ήταν μια ναζιστική οργάνωση με τάγματα εφόδου, ξυλοδαρμούς και δολοφονικές επιθέσεις. Δεν ξεχνάμε τους Αιγύπτιους αλιεργάτες, τους συνδικαλιστές του ΠΑΜΕ, τον Σαχζάτ Λουκμάν. Δεν ξεχνάμε τον Παύλο Φύσσα. Και δεν πρόκειται να αφήσουμε τη μνήμη αυτών των εγκλημάτων να ξεθωριάσει για να παρουσιαστούν ξανά οι ίδιοι άνθρωποι και οι ίδιες ιδέες ως κάτι «καινούργιο» ή «αντισυστημικό».


Απέναντι σε αυτή την απειλή δεν χωρά εφησυχασμός. Ο φασισμός δεν αντιμετωπίζεται με σιωπή και αναμονή. Αντιμετωπίζεται πολιτικά και μαζικά, στους χώρους δουλειάς, στις σχολές και στις γειτονιές, με οργάνωση, ταξική αλληλεγγύη και συλλογική δράση. Η αντιφασιστική πάλη δεν είναι τελετουργία μιας επετείου. Είναι καθημερινό μέτωπο απέναντι στο φασισμό, στον ρατσισμό και στις κοινωνικές συνθήκες που τους επιτρέπουν να σηκώνουν ξανά κεφάλι.


ΦΑΣΙΣΤΕΣ ΘΑ ΠΕΡΑΣΟΥΜΕ ΑΠΟ ΠΑΝΩ ΣΑΣ


 Αριστερή Κίνηση Περιστερίου


 ΟΙ ΝΑΖΙ ΔΕΝ ΕΧΟΥΝ ΘΕΣΗ ΣΤΙΣ ΓΕΙΤΟΝΙΕΣ ΜΑΣ


[

 ΑΝΤΙΦΑΣΙΣΤΙΚΗ ΔΙΑΔΗΛΩΣΗ ΣΤΟ ΠΕΡΙΣΤΕΡΙ ]


 Παρασκευή 16/10 στις 19:00, στην πλατεία Δημαρχείου


 Την Πέμπτη 8/10, νεοναζί έστησαν ενέδρα και μαχαίρωσαν αντιφασίστα στην Ελευσίνα.


 Το βράδυ της Δευτέρας 5/10, φασιστοειδή γέμισαν την πρόσοψη του στεκιού της Αριστερής Κίνησης Περιστερίου με ναζιστικά σύμβολα.


 Τις τελευταίες μέρες, φασίστες βάφουν τα σχολεία των δυτικών προαστίων με σβάστικες.


Οι ναζί μαχαιροβγάλτες κλιμακώνουν την προσπάθειά τους να επαναφέρουν στους δρόμους τα τάγματα εφόδου, και αυτό δεν είναι τυχαίο. Συμβαίνει παράλληλα με την υπερπροβολή της αποφυλάκισης Κασιδιάρη από τα ΜΜΕ, αλλά και με το σταθερό άνοιγμα της κυβέρνησης Μητσοτάκη στην ακροδεξιά.


 Καλούμε όλο τον κόσμο της πόλης να σταθεί απέναντι στο τέρας που θέλει να πατήσει το πόδι του στις γειτονιές μας !

title: Rojnameger Bahadir Ozgur bi şerte kontrol edlî serbest bû
content:
Nivîskar û bernamegerê Halk TVyê Bahadir Ozgurr duh(15ê Cotmehê) hatibû desteserkirin. 


Rêvebera Weşanê ya Giştî ya halktv.com.tryê Bengu Şap Babaekerê agahiya desteserkirinê li ser hesabê xwe yê Xê bi gotinên “Bahadir Ozgur tê desteserkirin” ragihand.


Ozgur îdîaya ku “nihêniya lêpirsîna fonê binpê kiriye” hat desteserkirin. Lêpirsîn ji aliyê Serdozgeriya Komarî ya Stenbolê ve tê birêvebirin.


Ozgur piştî karûbarên li Emniyetê îro ji bo Edliyeyê hat şandin. Dozgeriyê bi daxwaza şertê kontrola edlî û qedexeya derketina derve Ozgur sewqî dadgehê kir.


Dadgehê jî xwest ku Ozgur heftê de 2 caran li emniyetê îmzeyê bide û derketina derveyî welat lê qedexe kir û serbest berda.


Rojnameya Evrenselê nivîsî ku polîsan Ozgur birine Emniyeta Vatanê. Rojnameger Hakki Ozdal jî gotiye ku îfadeya Bahadir Ozgur a li emniyetê bi dawî bûye û dê di saetên sibehê de bibin adliyeyê.


Her weha hesabê Xê ê Bahadir Ozgur ku 163 hezar şopînerên wê hene (@bahadir_ozgr) hat astengkirin. Ev hesab hîn ji aliyê platforma Xê ve ji bo bikarhênerên li Tirkiyeyê nehatiye reş kirin.


Lîsteya di lêpirsînê de kiribû nûçe


Bahadir Ozgur di nûçeya xwe ya 13ê Cotmehê de diyar kiribû ku Serdozgeriya Komarî ya Stenbolê lîsteya tedbîrê ya mal û mulkên 141 kesan ku di nav wan de wezîra berê Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya û hevjînê wê İlyas Kaya jî hene, ji saziyên peywendîdar re şandiye.


Ozgurr nivîsîbû ku serdozgeriyê di 13ê Cotmehê de nivîseke nû şandiye û ragihandiye ku navên 29 kesan di lîsteyê de ‘bi xeletî’ cih girtine û diyar kiribû ku di nav van kesan de Enver Çevik û Kemal Akkaya jî hene.


Serdozgeriyê ragihand ku wan ev rewş bi nivîseke nû rast kiriye û tedbîrên li ser mal û mulkên 109 kesan berdewam dikin.


(VC/AY)

author: Unknown
title: Aksu: Ecology is better understood, but shallow approaches persist
content:
Ecological destruction and the plundering of nature are increasing day by day in Turkey and Kurdistan. As the environmental impact of projects carried out under the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government's “mega projects” is debated, the loss of forested areas continues.


Cemil Aksu of Polen Ecology spoke to ANF about the ecological destruction taking place in Turkey and Kurdistan, the causes of the plundering of nature and the struggle against it.


Aksu pointed out that 68 percent of forest destruction in Turkey has occurred under AKP rule and said: “The export-led growth strategy pursued by the AKP is turning Turkey into the West's Africa. Turkey's ecological problems began to escalate dramatically under AKP rule. The AKP started with ‘urban transformation’, ‘dual carriageways’, ‘megacities’ and ‘mega projects’, turning the entire country into a construction site. To supply the energy, cement and other raw materials needed for this construction site, it also turned rural areas, valleys and rivers across the country into sites for energy production, mining and other activities.


Global Forest Watch (GFW) data show that Turkey lost a total of 840,000 hectares of tree cover between 2001 and 2025, equivalent to approximately 8 percent of its tree cover area in 2000. In 2025 alone, 51,000 hectares of natural forest were lost. Professor Erdoğan Atmış's 2024 assessment is even more striking: the area legally or effectively deforested has exceeded 1.5 million hectares, and at least 68 percent of this resulted from land allocations made under AKP rule. Energy and mining rank first among the causes.


Over the past five or six years, a new wave of destruction has emerged. This new wave of extractivism is led by large-scale mining projects, including cyanide-based gold mining, oil and natural gas exploration using hydraulic fracturing, and rare earth element mining.


The government wants to turn the steps taken by the US-led Western imperialist bloc in its new struggle to divide up the world against Russia and China into an opportunity to transform the imperial legacy inherited by the Turkish bourgeoisie from the Ottoman Empire into a vision for the future. This neo-Ottomanism is not an AKP project; it is part of the historical consciousness of the Turkish bourgeoisie. The discourse of ‘the Turkish world from the Adriatic to the Great Wall of China’ predates the AKP and extends beyond it.


In the previous period, they made certain manoeuvres within the magnetic field between the US and Russia. But in the new phase that began with Russia's defeat in Syria, the government rapidly changed its position and became Trump's close ally. Over the past decade, particularly through advances in the arms industry, they have sought to secure a significant place in the emerging global system and gain an economic advantage over rivals of comparable strength. To achieve this, they are trying to benefit from the sanctions imposed on Russia and China by the US and other Western imperialist powers, positioning Turkey as a supply hub for certain essential intermediate goods and raw materials.


To this end, they are particularly seeking to expand the production of raw materials needed by digital technologies and the arms industry. This is also something Trump wants. It could even be said that the ‘super permit law’, passed by parliament last year and granting major advantages to mining companies, was enacted at Trump's direct request.


According to the Extractivism Report prepared by the Polen Ecology Collective, the areas allocated to companies over the past four years have exceeded one million hectares. In 2026 alone, an area larger than eight of the country's provinces was handed over to capital. A total of 266 districts where mining, oil and natural gas activities are concentrated were identified as ‘sacrifice zones’.


In Maraş, eight districts were included on the list: the central district, Göksun, Çağlayancerit, Onikişubat, Afşin, Elbistan, Pazarcık and Nurhak. In Gümüşhane, Torul, the central district, Kürtün, Kelkit and Şiran were identified as ‘sacrifice zones’, along with Küre, Bozkurt, Çatalzeytin, Taşköprü, the central district, Pınarbaşı and Tosya in Kastamonu.


In Kütahya, nine districts were included on the list: Emet, Gediz, Simav, Şaphane, Domaniç, Tavşanlı, the central district, Altıntaş and Aslanapa. The capital was not spared the expansion of mining either. Ankara's districts of Kızılcahamam, Çubuk, Haymana …

title: No news of artist Jîna Ehmedî, arrested in Iran, for 10 days
content:
There has been no news for 10 days of artist Jîna Ehmedî, also known as Jîlemo, who was detained by Iranian regime forces in the city of Merîwan in Eastern Kurdistan.


According to Kolber News, Jîna Ehmedî, who is from the village of Nigil in the Merîwan area, was detained by Iranian regime forces at her home in Merîwan. She was subsequently taken to Sine Central Prison. Despite 10 days having passed since her detention, no information has been obtained about her health or whereabouts.


It has been reported that Ehmedî is being held in the women's ward of the prison and has been denied the right to meet with her lawyer, communicate by telephone, or meet with her family in person.


She provided art education to children


Jîna Ehmedî is known as the founder of Jîlemo Music House, which operates in Merîwan.


No explanation has been given for the reasons behind Ehmedî's detention. She founded the institution, which provides children with education in music, singing, painting, and cinema.

author: Ed Wanderley
title: Um jumento na filarmônica
content:
De orelhas sempre de pé e com uma zurra que ecoa por mais de 3 km entre a vegetação, talvez o jumento não seja a associação mais óbvia que se pense em relação ao universo da música. E, no entanto, aos 33 anos, Antonino Tertulino está mais do que habituado a preencher as caixas mais improváveis.


“Eu me considero um jumento. E eu tenho essa visão, pois nunca penso em ser uma peça de destaque. Aqueles que são muito presenteados, muito exigidos, e como o jumento é subestimado, passa despercebido, sabe?”

, conta o jovem magro de cabelos rareando, cujo talento diante de um contrabaixo acústico, já exibido perante ao menos três presidentes e dois papas, há muito, não o deixa passar tão despercebido quanto tenta se enxergar.


No dia 19 de julho, Antonino deixou a Áustria, onde integrava a Orquestra Filarmônica de Salzburgo, para uma semana de passeio pela memória, no Recife, onde nasceu, um compromisso que se tornou regular em seu calendário anual.


Entre as paredes do Teatro de Santa Isabel, templo cultural que, desde a metade do século 19, se fez palco nobre da sociedade pernambucana, ele foi um dos músicos a capitanear uma sequência de apresentações da Orquestra Criança Cidadã, formada por estudantes de 6 a 21 anos, na qual ele mesmo, vinte anos antes, teve sua iniciação no mundo da música. O trote silencioso de Antonino ecoa. O zurro é de gratidão, mas os olhares ao redor são mesmo aspiracionais. O contrabaixista tirou tempo para estar junto das crianças, conceder entrevistas e reencontrar amigos.


O ritual se deu antes dos preparativos para mudar de casa mais uma vez, agora para desbravar a Alemanha, onde acaba de assinar com a

Niederbayerische Philharmonie

, de Landshut.

 “Uma das dezessete melhores do mundo”, diz uma das vozes contemplativas no interior do teatro, fazendo jus à megalomania pernambucana, sempre disposta a um ranking que nem sequer carece de fontes. 


A impressão dos que o acompanham é que a carreira de Antonino não tem um limite claro de até onde pode chegar e que segue em rota ascendente, sempre em frente, sem desvios. Quem é do interior, sabe: jumentos têm excelente senso de direção.


Antonino em 7 notas


DO

is coelhos com uma cajadada


Fugir das aulas de física e química. Essa foi a primeira intenção de um Antonino de 13 anos, ainda em 2006, admite o hoje músico, em retrospecto. Aos alunos da Escola Nossa Senhora do Carmo, logo após a apresentação de um quinteto de cordas, foi oferecida a oportunidade de concorrer a uma das vagas do projeto Orquestra Criança Cidadã.


A escolha da unidade de ensino no Coque não foi por acaso. A região do bairro Joana Bezerra carecia de infraestrutura básica e tinha uma pobreza hostil que, muitas vezes, era retratada apenas pela face da violência.

 Não por menos, o discurso padrão era o de resgate, oferecendo atividades para que os alunos jovens não tivessem tempo de serem capturados pelo trabalho infantil ou cooptados pelo tráfico – e, entre os atrativos, estavam acompanhamento médico e odontológico, bem como refeições regulares.  


As aulas de música seriam no contraturno do calendário escolar, nas dependências do 7º Depósito de Suprimentos do Exército. Como incentivo, a atividade representaria horas de aula – o que, para o garoto, seria uma chance de se livrar das matérias que, àquela altura, já lhe causavam dor de cabeça. O impulso inicial, no entanto, deu lugar à admiração pelo novo mundo.


“Algo que me deixou bem curioso foi a comunicação entre os músicos, sem nenhuma comunicação verbal, sabe? Hoje, com colegas, eu faço isso no dia a dia, na orquestra, essa comunicação de gesto, de olhar, tudo. Mas aquilo teve um efeito “uau” pra mim, de como eles agiam como um time.”


As crianças da região, a partir dos seis anos, foram convidadas a realizar testes de aptidão musical facilitados. O desafio consistia em uma melodia de solfejo e em um método rítmico simplificado. Aprovados, eles seriam divididos entre os instrumentos – e as atenções se voltaram todas ao violino. 


“E eu dizia: ‘aquele ali, rapaz, pelo tamanho, vai ser difícil de controlar’. Se o violino é difícil, aquele ali é ainda mais difícil, pelo tamanho.’ E eu sempre fui franzino, assim, magrinho, né?”

, lembra Antonino. Desde então, a relação com o instrumento se fez como complemento de si mesmo e da própria imagem que tentava projetar.

author: dialogocomospovos
title: II Raízes - A Gameleira  é Planta Sagrada!
content:
Cacique Juvenal Payayá fala sobre a gameleira, planta sagrada para seu povo. Ele explica que a gameleira é árvore própria da Caatinga, que sempre deu na beira das águas, e que seu significado sagrado é histórico. O local onde hoje acontece o encontro, na cabeceira do Rio Utinga, foi o palco da mais cruenta batalha que fomentou a chamada Guerra dos Bárbaros. Depois de massacrar os Payayá, os invasores deram um ponto final àquele nome. A região era habitada pelos Payayá, e a mata que existe ali já foi plantio deles.


Cacique Juvenal conta que, naquele lugar, havia um pé de gameleira. Para construir a barragem, derrubaram a árvore com machado — para ele, o último golpe no processo de apagamento histórico. As avós foram apanhadas, tiveram seus nomes trocados: tia Gita não se chamava Gita, avó Maria não se chamava Maria, avó Duninha não se chamava Duninha. Todas passaram a ser Ana, Maria, Francisca, nomes de santas. Elas resistiram e passaram a ser chamadas de gameleira, pela atenção que davam àquela árvore imensa, de raízes triangulares, mais altas que uma mão levantada, que seguravam um tronco maior.


Mesmo derrubada, logo ali na frente um novo pé de gameleira nasceu. O povo Payayá o cultiva com carinho e transformou a filha da gameleira em sua raiz sagrada.


Cacique Juvenal pede que guardem essa história e que pesquisadores a estudem: há muito ainda a ser descoberto. A gameleira que insiste em brotar é como a resistência do povo Payayá, o 15º povo indígena da Bahia.

title: Community care needs time
content:
Community care takes time and energy that rising rents and the cost of living leave people without. The speaker describes people working two and three jobs, and points to the idea of community care as something to pursue as far as possible: take care of each other and organize collectively, in solidarity. The ask that follows is to liberate our time and work less, so there is more time to care for friends and families.

author: Unknown
title: 6e assemblée anticarcérale paname et environs : 25 Octobre à la Parole Errante !
content:
La sixième Assemblée Anticarcérale Paname & Environs aura lieu le dimanche 25 Octobre à la parole errante (9 Rue François Debergue, Montreuil). Le lieu sera ouvert dès 15h30 pour s'installer, écrire ensemble des lettres à des prisonnier·es ou parcourir l'infokiosque, et l'assemblée même commencera à 16h. On conseille d'essayer autant que possible de venir sans téléphone (ou au pire, de l'éteindre en avance) pour réduire la surveillance que l'on s'impose à travers l'omniprésence des mouchards technologiques dans nos milieux. Il y aura aussi un coin et des activités pour les enfants, pour permettre aux personnes qui ont des enfants de pouvoir participer à l'assemblée.


L'assemblée anti carcérale paris & environs a pour vocation d'être un espace d'organisation ouvert se réunissant mensuellement afin d'agir collectivement en solidarité avec les mouvements des prisonnier.es et tisser des liens avec les prisonnier.es et leurs proches sans passer par des cadres partisans ou syndicaux.


Lors des dernières grosses révoltes qui ont eu lieu, la réalité sociale de la répression nous a laissé-es face à un constat amer : nous sommes bien loin d'avoir les outils nécessaires pour réagir correctement face à l'appareil d'État, ainsi qu'amplifier la voix des prisonnier·ères et de celleux qui font les frais du système carcéral.


Pourtant, les mouvements ne manquent pas d'inventivité pour s'opposer de front aux prisons, que ce soit par des actions telles que l'attaque de la prison de Fresnes lors des révoltes de 2023, les attaques répétées de comicos dans cette même révolte comme lors des gilets jaunes, ou encore les attaques et intimidations de matons à domicile comme lors de

DDPF

.


Nous voulons nous en inspirer pour pousser nos luttes anti-carcérales plus loin, à la fois pour dépasser nos milieux anarchistes et adopter une position qui ne soit pas simplement défensive, en simple réaction à la répression.


La prison est — et sera toujours — l'un des symbole les plus éloquents de la puissance de l'État, de sa capacité à réprimer, enfermer et isoler l'ensemble des individu·es qui menacent son existence. La prison est au centre même de l'appareil colonial qui constitue l'État français : elle sert à mater et punir les révoltes des colonies comme récemment en Kanaky, Guadeloupe ou Martinique, à intensifier le tri aux frontières comme à Mayotte, et à tracer des frontières intérieures en incarcérant massivement les populations racisées, colonisées et les plus pauvres.


Attaquer les lieux d'incarcération - par les mots, la solidarité, le feu ou la bombe - c'est alors s'attaquer à ses outils privilégiés.


Rompre l'isolement des/avec les détenu·es est alors devenu rapidement pour les mouvements anticarcéraux un moyen d'affaiblir l'appareil carcéral et l'État colonial. En exposant la voix des personnes enfermé·es, on se donne le moyen de penser «

 

la prison

 

» (son fonctionnement, ses outils, etc.), mais aussi de la rendre moins «

 

extérieure à nos vies

 

». Des surgissements tels que

DDPF

 ou les révoltes pour Nahel parviennent à la remettre au centre de l'attention en s'y attaquant ouvertement, créant des fissures dans lesquelles nous désirons nous engouffrer pour mettre fin à la trop commune realité de l'incarcération et des assassinats policiers.


Une des prouesse des États dits «

 

démocratiques

 

», est d'avoir réussi à faire de la notion d'enfermement un impensé pour toute une partie de la population. Une situation si lointaine que l'on ne prend même pas la peine de l'envisager, alors que c'est pourtant le quotidien de beaucoup de personnes...


Cette nécessité de destruction est d'autant plus présente dans une région parisienne qui concentre à elle seule une densité collossale d'institutions d'enfermements : que ce soit les taules, tribunaux, comicos, ou prisons pour sans-papiers, mineur-es, enfants, fols, tox, handi-es, animaux non-humains...


Pour nous, s'organiser signifie construire des nouvelles formes de lutte, de solidarité et de décision, par notre capacité collective à rompre avec l'ordre existant, à expérimenter, à créer, à inventer...


Depuis le début du 20

e

 siècle, les Anarchist Black Cross (

ABC

) et leurs réseaux ont cet avantage de se présenter sous une forme autonome et souple, fondée sur un internationalisme radicalement anti-carcéral, d'où notre envie de nous réaproprier cette forme et de s'inscrire dans un réseau pour abattre les prisons proches de chez nous comme à l'autre bout du …

title: Rojnameger Murat Agirel hat desteserkirin
content:

author: winter oak
title: For life and truth: his struggle was his success
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


Sigmund Kvaløy Setreng (1934-2014)

 was a philosopher and activist who was deeply opposed to what he termed the Industrial Growth Society – IGS.


We live, he

warned

 in 1993, in “a global robber economy, a systematic plundering of the earth’s last resources at an exponential rate”.


“Like so many of my own generation in Norway, I have experienced a complete transformation of society in one lifetime – from an almost medieval, agricultural self-reliant society to a modern super industrialism, replete with computers, holidays at Mallorca, and complete dependency on world market forces…


“The industrial transformation was slow at first, and throughout the first half of this century people largely went along with the hydroprojects, feeling that electricity and industrialization would compensate for the river losses.


“But after World War II all that changed: the schemes grew out of all reasonable proportions and far beyond the needs of the people. That’s when Norwegian electricity finally became the bridgehead for modern international big industry”. [1]


This imperial pillaging obviously

had

 a destructive impact on Norway’s magnificent landscape: “IGS tries to transform all mountainous areas and river sheds into gigantic cisterns for the production of industrial energy”. [2]


But Kvaløy Setreng also stressed the ill effects on the lives, culture and happiness of the Norwegian people. He wrote: “The deterioration of taste in half a generation coincides strikingly with the industrialization of the country. The state of aesthetic taste must somehow be the fruit of the transition to an IGS society”. [3]


And he

added

 in 2007: “Small-scale farming and fishing is being replaced by a tourist economy where exotic folklore on abandoned farms is taking the place of food production and computer games are replacing real games.


“It should be of interest to note that exactly in parallel with this development the rate of suicides has grown tremendously in Norway, now being one of the highest in the world”. [4]


Kvaløy Setreng described how modern urban society is designed to serve the demands of the rapacious “techno-capitalist economy” which cannot function without treating human beings in a supposedly rational and entirely “quantitative” manner.


Stripped of meaningful work and reduced to the slave-like status of dependent and obedient employees, people “gradually and unnoticeably

lose the ability

 to master their own situation and to take part in a conscious shaping of their society. In other words, we reach a state of affairs where people

have

 to be governed from the outside and above… Society becomes ‘addicted to’ a continuation on the same course”. [5]


“We see today a great drive to centralize people from the rural communities and the small towns into the great metropolis. The planners are at work, creating vast suburbs from scratch, pouring people into the quickly finished product.


“It is not taken into consideration that these people come from different backgrounds and different kinds of communities, and that they arrive with their ‘roots in mother earth’s soil’ torn off…


“The majority inhabiting the bottom sector of the IGS power pyramid

cannot be allowed

 to develop an ego-complexity anywhere nearly as strong as their leaders, because that would mean their effective refusal to function as quantities; then they could not be programmed, and statistical forecasts would break down all the time.


“The most functional citizen of IGS is one with no protruding edges – one who has the slippery shape of a simple disc – well suited to slide through the centrally designed pipe system of modern techno-society”. [6]


In contrast to this dehumanised industrial society, Kvaløy Setreng

presented

 the idea of a “

livsnødvendighetssamfunnet

 (“life necessities society”, LNS) a society characterized by solidarity, autonomous small communities and the production of only the necessities of life. [7]


He

explained

: “The top of the IGS pyramid, seen as a centralized social organization, may also be compared to the governing station of a machine – the single position from which you start and stop it and control all its functions.


“It is a basic characteristic of a machine to have just one such control center, while a

living, organic

 process has many, or you might say, none: the whole is governing itself”. [8]

title: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan - Will 1793 Take Place?
content:
Author

: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan

Title

: Will 1793 Take Place?

Subtitle

: Destituent Remarks on the Chilean Uprising and the Yellow Vests

Date

: October 6

th

, 2026

Notes

: Translated by the authors and Ill Will

Source

: https://illwill.com/1793


 


 First published in French in August 2026, the present article argues that the 2018–19 Yellow Vests movement in France and the 2019 Chilean uprising form two instances of a single pattern. In each case, an insurrection begins with modest demands, such as a metro fare or a fuel tax only to then explode outward, outstripping its own stated goals, before ultimately being contained by constituent processes, referendums, and left-wing electoral projects. The authors treat the Constitution of 1793, with its famous article on the “duty of insurrection,” as the archetypal “act of capture” for such sequences: on the one hand, it was an attempt by ruling powers to absorb revolutionary energy into itself; at the same time, it served to embed a permanent insurrectionary principle into the political-legal system, one which the state has never been able to fully extirpate. Against the left’s push for new constitutional initiatives, the authors argue for a “revolution without power” grounded in the refusal of institutions and representation, crediting the Yellow Vests with developing new forms of assembly and fleeting affiliation in the absence of a distinct language or subject of its own. The key question, they suggest, is ultimately not whether 1793 will take place, but who will finish the job.


 


 Then annihilate forever what may one day destroy your work. Consider that the fruit of your labors being reserved for your grandchildren only, duty and probity command that you bequeath them none of those seeds of disaster which could mean for your descendants a renewal of the chaos whence we have with so much trouble just emerged. At the present moment our prejudices are weakening; the people have already abjured the Catholic absurdities; they have already suppressed the temples, sent the relics flying, and agreed that marriage is a mere civil undertaking; the smashed confessionals serve as public meeting places; the former faithful, deserting the apostolic banquet, leave the gods of flour dough to the mice. […] One more effort; since you labor to destroy all the old foundations, do not permit one of them to survive, for let but one endure, ‘tis enough, the rest will be restored. And how much more certain of their revival must we not be if the one you tolerate is positively the source and cradle of all the others! —Marquis de Sade,

Philosophy in the Bedroom

, 1795


In Santiago as in Paris


 Chile, October 25

th

, 2020.

[1]

 After months of insurrectionary demonstrations, the government agrees to hold a referendum to elect a constituent assembly. The vote takes place on the 15

th

 and 16

th

 of May, 2021, and on July 4

th

 the assembly begins its work, which is to last for a period of one year. With the initiation of the constituent process, another quite distinct process draws to a close: the revolutionary process. The latter began on October 7, 2019 when groups of young people, dissatisfied with the rise in metro fares, decided to refuse to pay and to jump the ticket barriers en masse. Collective ingenuity, the joy of rebellion, the determination of the

primera línea

 (frontline), the feeling of being on the verge of storming heaven, all gradually give way to self-serious protocols and democratic formalism. On two separate occasions, the newly drafted constitution is rejected in referendums and abandoned. The rest is history: the left wins the elections of November–December 2021 with an abstention rate of roughly 50 percent, taking power in March 2022. Yet the aftermath proves disappointing and, in December 2025, a far-right candidate, the son of a Nazi, is elected as the country’s leader against a backdrop of a spectacular rise in voter turnout (up thirty-eight percent in the first round, and twenty-nine in the second). Once again, hopes for a Chilean path towards a freer and more egalitarian society are dashed. Once again, counterrevolution succeeds in stifling the revolutionary process, by imposing upon it the timeframe and institutional forms of democratic power: the mirage of a referendum, a moment of national electoral unity, a left-wing government, and a breakthrough by the far right.

title: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan - Remarks on the Ongoing Student Revolt
content:
Author

: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan

Title

: Remarks on the Ongoing Student Revolt

Date

: October 9

th

, 2026

Notes

: Translated by Ill Will

Source

: https://illwill.com/remarks-on-the-ongoing-student-revolt


 The following remarks, forged in the heat of battle during a wave of student unrest that is now spreading to Belgium and Italy, were posted to

x.com

 on October 6, 2026. For a longer position piece by the same authors, see their recent article, “

Will 1793 Take Place?

”


1.


 The student revolt is the spearhead of the movement announced for October 17.


2.


 The “gangs” [bandes] of students from working-class neighborhoods constitute the actual driving force both within and against the current youth movement. In a sense, this force is less a part of the student movement than it is a continuation of the Nahel revolt. It has neither demands nor representatives; it does not conform to the codes of the Left and rejects bourgeois politeness. It wants revenge.


3.


 The universities have followed the high schools and joined the dynamic of the blockades. They, in turn, could bring about a qualitative leap by, for example, launching an occupation that could be taken up and spread by other sectors of society—whether students or not. This hypothesis, however, is oppposed by the overwhelming dominance of student union organizations, which leave little room for group spontaneity, collective ingenuity, and self-subversive practices.


4.


 When one speaks of “blockades” at high schools, one is already engaging in a form of reduction and simplification of the practices of the student revolt. There are acts of sabotage (doors set on fire, gates knocked down, “e-blockades” against distance learning) and acts of revenge (against the school hierarchy and the police outside), urban guerrilla tactics (barricades) and wildcat strikes (work stoppages during breaks and staggered blockades), and finally something akin to a game aimed at ridiculing authority (slogans about Macron and his teacher, superhero costumes in contrast to the oppressors’ uniforms).


5.


 The unions cannot come to terms with the idea of October 17, as it reminds them too much of the Yellow Vests. They must pretend to join the movement in order to gain better control over it—both through their monopoly on negotiations and by dictating the timeline. If the inter-union coalition called for action on October 6 alongside the students, it was only to better defuse the call for October 17, which they wish to reduce to an interim date ahead of their mobilization on November 5.


6.


 In high schools, the left differs from other political forces in form, but not in substance. In form, the left pushes students into the role of victims, thereby allowing itself to present as the “responsible adults.” Consider the human chains of parents and teachers, or elected officials denouncing the police’s use of LBD weapons. It is striking, however, that batons, shields, helmets, and other standard components of the arsenal of democracy are far less frequently called into question.


7.


 In terms of substance, the left aligns itself with the other political forces in their efforts to restore peace. This is precisely what happens when it puts forward demands that are consistent with its platform, thereby helping to separate the “good” students (those with demands deemed legitimate) from the “bad” students (these “rioters” without ideas or genuine political motives).


8.


 Unlike the left, we have neither flags to wave, nor a tempo to set, nor lessons to teach.


9.


 How should we deal with the enthusiasm for “October 17” and the way certain segments of the youth present it as an echo of the Yellow Vests movement? Even if a new generation seems to invoke its symbolic power full of hope, it is by no means certain that reusing the object will help us rediscover its spirit. Nevertheless, perhaps that is precisely what is expected of us: to don it and see if it—even if only temporarily—embodies a sense of belonging with which others can identify and to which they can align themselves, without appropriating it in the process. At the risk of appearing ridiculous and anachronistic, and discarding it again swiftly.


10.


 The spectacular actions of the student revolt are the work of bands or gangs [bandes] that organize themselves and make their identity known in this way. Wearing Under Armour outfits fools no one: only to the extent that we reconnect …
